title: Dancing Queen
summary: The song tells the story of a woman who realizes she has lost her youth and is now an older woman, but she can still remember the good times when she was younger. summary: The song's lyrics are about a woman who is trying to determine which of three men (Mamma Mia) is her father. The chorus repeats the phrase 'Mamma mia', and the song has become one of ABBA's most popular and enduring songs.

title: S.O.S.

summary: Swan Lake is a classical ballet composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky. The music includes the famous 'Dance of the Little Swans' and the dramatic 'Black Swan Pas de Deux'. The piece is considered one of Tchaikovsky's most iconic works.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 1 in B-flat minor, Op. 23 is a piano concerto by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky. Composed between May and August 1875, the concerto was dedicated to Russian pianist Nikolai Rubinstein, who had given Tchaikovsky some valuable advice on its composition. The work premiered in Boston in 1888 and London in 1894. A concerto for piano and orchestra, it consists of three movements: Allegro non troppo e molto maestoso - Andante semplice - Allegro con spirito.

title: Nocturne in E-flat major
summary: The Nocturne in E-flat major, Op. 9, No. 2, is a nocturne by Frédéric Chopin. It was written around 1830-1832 and published posthumously in 1846.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 2 in F minor, Op. 21 is a concerto for solo piano and orchestra composed by Frédéric Chopin. The work was written between September 1830 and February 1831. It is considered one of the most technically challenging works in the classical piano repertoire.

title: La Campanella
summary: La Campanella (Italian for 'The Little Bell') is a piano piece by Franz Liszt, composed in 1832. The piece is based on the famous theme from Paganini's Caprice No. 9, and it features a bell-like melody. La Campanella is considered one of Liszt's most technically challenging pieces and requires great skill to play.

title: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2
summary: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 is a famous piano piece by Franz Liszt, composed in 1839. It's part of the Hungarian Rhapsodies series and showcases Liszt's mastery of chromaticism and virtuosity. The piece has become an iconic representation of Hungarian folk music, with its dramatic and expressive qualities.

title: Water Music Suite No. 1
summary: The Water Music is a collection of orchestral suites composed by George Frideric Handel in 1717 for the king of England, George I. It was written to celebrate the King's barge trip on the River Thames. The suite is characterized by its lively and majestic music, with intricate instrumental passages.

title: Messiah (Hallelujah Chorus)
summary: The 'Hallelujah Chorus' is one of the most recognizable and beloved pieces of choral music in the world. It is a part of George Frideric Handel's oratorio 'Messiah', written for Easter 1741 but first performed on April 13, 1742, at the New Music Hall in Fishamble Street, Dublin. The piece is known for its majestic and celebratory tone, with a grand chorus accompanied by an orchestra.

title: La Traviata
summary: La Traviata is an opera in three acts by Giuseppe Verdi, based on Alexandre Dumas' novel La Dame aux Camélias. The story revolves around the life of Violetta Valéry, a courtesan who falls in love with Alfredo Germont, but must choose between her loyalty to him and her duty to society.

title: Aida
summary: Aida is an opera in four acts, written by Giuseppe Verdi for the Khedivial Opera House in Cairo. The libretto was adapted by Antonio Ghislanzoni from a French novel called Aida and Mariette (1857).

title: Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg (Overture)
summary: The opera Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg is a comedic tale of love, pride, and redemption set in 16th-century Nuremberg. The overture is a famous and iconic piece that introduces the main themes of the opera.

title: Ride of the Valkyries
summary: The Ride of the Valkyries is a famous orchestral piece from Richard Wagner's opera Die Walküre, the second installment in his epic music drama cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen. The music depicts the Valkyries flying over the battlefield on their horses, selecting half of those who have fallen to take to Valhalla for a heroic death. The piece is known for its soaring strings and powerful brass sections, creating an unforgettable effect.

title: Sonata in G minor for Violin and Continuo
summary: The Sonata in G minor for Violin and Continuo is a sonata written by Italian composer Giuseppe Tartini. It is considered one of his most famous works, known for its expressive and emotional qualities. The sonata consists of three movements: a fast and energetic first movement, a slow and melancholic second movement, and a lively and playful third movement.

title: Devil's Trill Sonata (Sonata in A minor)
summary: The Devil's Trill is a sonata for solo violin composed by Giuseppe Tartini. It is considered one of the most technically challenging and beautiful pieces in the violin repertoire. The sonata consists of three movements, each with its own unique character. The first movement is marked by a strong rhythmic pulse and dramatic contrasts. The second movement is a lyrical slow movement that showcases the expressive qualities of the violin. The third movement is a lively finale that features rapid arpeggios and virtuosic fingerwork.

title: La Follia
summary: La Follia (The Madness) is a violin concerto suite composed by Arcangelo Corelli. It consists of 12 variations on the same theme, each with its own unique character and mood. The piece showcases Corelli's mastery of counterpoint and his ability to create complex, yet beautiful music.

title: Christmas Concerto
summary: The Christmas Concerto (Concerto Grossi No. 8, Op. 6, No. 8) is a musical composition by Arcangelo Corelli, published in 1690. It is a festive and celebratory piece, featuring a large orchestra and showcasing the composer's mastery of the concerto grosso form. The work consists of five movements: Allegro, Adagio, Allegro, Minuetto, and Allegro.

title: Lamento della Ninfa
summary: This piece is a lament sung by the nymph in Claudio Monteverdi's opera 'Il Ritorno d'Ulisse in Patria'. The nymph laments the loss of her love, Ulisse. The music is characterized by its expressive and dramatic qualities, with a focus on vocal declamation and expressive ornamentation.

title: Combattimento di Tancredi e Clorinda
alternative_title: The Combat of Tancred and Clorinda
summary: The Combattimento di Tancredi e Clorinda (Combat of Tancred and Clorinda) is a dramatic madrigal written by Claudio Monteverdi in 1624. It tells the story of Tancred, an Italian knight who falls in love with Clorinda, a Saracen princess, but their love is doomed. The work is considered one of Monteverdi's masterpieces and a landmark in the development of opera. It is set to a text by Ottavio Rinuccini, based on Torquato Tasso's epic poem Jerusalem Delivered.

title: Dido's Lament
summary: A lament by Dido, the queen of Carthage from Virgil's Aeneid. The song is sung by Aeneas' lover, who has been abandoned and is mourning his departure.

title: King Arthur's Funeral Music
summary: A somber and reflective piece of music, King Arthur's Funeral Music is a lament for the death of King Arthur. Composed by Henry Purcell in 1691, this beautiful and poignant piece is characterized by its slow and mournful melody, evoking a sense of sadness and loss. The music is based on the legend of King Arthur's demise and serves as a eulogy to the great king.

title: Lagrime di San Pietro
summary: Lagrime di San Pietro (Tears of Saint Peter) is a collection of madrigals by Orlando di Lasso, written in the late 16th century. The work is based on a series of poems by Marcantonio Flaminio and consists of five books, each containing several madrigals.

title: Requiem Mass for Edward VI
summary: A setting of the traditional Latin Requiem Mass, written by Orlando di Lasso in memory of King Edward VI of England. The work is notable for its beauty and complexity, featuring intricate polyphonic textures and a sense of mournfulness. While there are no lyrics per se, the text is taken from the Latin mass for the dead and sets the tone for a somber and reflective mood.

title: Sicut cervus
summary: A sacred motet for four voices, written by the renowned Italian composer Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina. The text is a biblical verse (Psalm 42:1), and the music features Palestrina's characteristic expressive counterpoint.

title: Tu es Petrus
summary: Tu es Petrus is a motet by Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina, composed in the late 16th century. The piece is written for six voices and is based on the Gospel of Matthew (16:18). It is considered one of Palestrina's most famous compositions and is still widely performed today.

title: Orfeo ed Euridice: Che farò senza Euridice?
summary: Che farò senza Euridice is a famous aria from Christoph Willibald Gluck's opera Orfeo ed Euridice. The aria is sung by Orpheus, who has lost his wife Eurydice to death and is left to lament her loss. He asks himself what he will do without her, and the aria becomes a powerful expression of love and longing. The music is known for its beautiful melody and Gluck's innovative use of recitative to create a sense of drama and emotion.

title: Alceste: Ah! Mio cor non sia più tradito
summary: Ah! mio cor non sia più tradito (Ah, my heart may never be betrayed) is a soprano aria from Christoph Willibald Gluck's opera Alceste. The libretto was written by Ranieri de Calzabigi and the music composed by Gluck in 1767. This aria showcases the beauty of the human voice as it conveys intense emotions.

title: "Te Deum"
summary: The Te Deum, H.146, is a large-scale sacred choral work by Jean-Baptiste Lully, composed in 1694 to celebrate the French naval victories of Louis XIV. The piece is known for its grandeur and opulence, with complex harmonies and intricate instrumental arrangements.

title: "Armide"
summary: Armide is a tragic opera by French composer Jean-Baptiste Lully, first performed in Paris on February 15, 1686. The libretto was written by Philippe Quinault and based on Torquato Tasso's epic poem 'Jerusalem Delivered'. The opera tells the story of Armida, a sorceress who falls in love with Renaud, a Christian knight. The work is known for its dramatic intensity, expressive music, and innovative use of orchestration.

title: The Triumph of Time and Love
summary: The Triumph of Time and Love is a suite for harpsichord by French Baroque composer François Couperin. The piece is known for its complex counterpoint and intricate musical patterns, showcasing the composer's mastery of Baroque music.

title: Les Bergeries
summary: This piece, composed by Franôis Couperin, is a collection of four suites for the harpsichord. Each suite contains several movements that showcase different emotions and moods, including calmness, elegance, and even a bit of playfulness. The title "Les Bergeries" translates to "The Shepherds' Huts," evoking images of serene countryside settings.

title: Extase
summary: Extase (Euphoria) is a poem by Victor Hugo, set to music by Henri Duparc. The poem describes the feeling of being in a state of euphoria, where one's senses are heightened and they feel connected to nature. The music is characterized by long, flowing melodies and a sense of calm.

title: Phidylé
summary: Phidylé is a song by French composer Henri Duparc, set to the poetry of Victor Hugo. The song features a beautiful melody and poignant lyrics, evoking a sense of longing and nostalgia.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2
alternative_title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in C minor, Op. 18
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 2 is one of Rachmaninoff's most popular works. It consists of three movements: the first movement, marked Adagio sostenuto, is a slow and introspective introduction; the second movement, a Scherzo, is a lively and playful contrast; and the third movement, Praeludium - Allegro scherzando, is a rapid and energetic conclusion. The concerto is known for its technical challenges and emotional depth.

title: The Rite of Spring
summary: The Rite of Spring is a ballet with a score by Igor Stravinsky, first performed in Paris on May 29, 1913. It was a groundbreaking work that shocked audiences with its radical departure from traditional classical music.

title: Firebird Suite
summary: The Firebird Suite, originally known as L'Oiseau de Feu, is a ballet composed by Igor Stravinsky. The suite was first performed in 1910 and it is based on the Russian fairy tale 'The Firebird' by Alexander Afanasyev.

title: Flight of the Bumblebee
summary: A well-known excerpt from Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov's opera 'The Tale of Tsar Saltan', featuring a rapid arpeggio pattern that mimics the flight of a bumblebee.

title: Scheherazade, Moods Tingited by the Night of the Harem
alternative_title: Scheherazade: Moods Tingited by the Night of the Harem
summary: Scheherazade is a famous musical composition based on One Thousand and One Nights, an ancient Middle Eastern folk tale. The piece is divided into ten tableaux and features orchestral suites with beautiful instrumental melodies, evoking the exotic atmosphere of the harem.

title: Night on Bald Mountain
summary: Based on a Russian folk tale, the piece depicts a supernatural night on Bald Mountain where witches and demons gather to dance. The music is known for its dramatic and haunting qualities, with complex harmonies and rhythms that evoke a sense of darkness and foreboding.

title: Pictures at an Exhibition - The Old Castle
summary: The third movement of Pictures at an Exhibition, composed by Modest Mussorgsky in 1874. The piece is a musical depiction of the illustrations for the album 'Pictures at an Exhibition' and is one of the most famous pieces from this collection.

title: Symphony No. 9 "From the New World"
summary: Dvořák's Symphony No. 9, also known as From the New World, is a symphony in four movements composed by Antonín Dvořák between 1892 and 1893. The work was written during his time in the United States, where he had moved from Bohemia to serve as director of the National Conservatory of Music of America. The symphony's themes are believed to have been inspired by African-American spirituals, Native American melodies, and other folk influences.

title: Carnival Overture
summary: The Carnival Overture is a musical composition by Antonín Dvořák, written in 1892. It is an overture that evokes the spirit of a carnival with its lively rhythms and melodic motifs.

title: The Bartered Bride
summary: The Bartered Bride (Czech: Prodaná nevěsta) is a comic opera in three acts, composed by Bedřich Smetana to a Czech libretto by Karel Sabina. It premiered on September 8, 1866, at the National Theatre in Prague. The story revolves around Johnicka and Jenik, two lovers who are forced into an arranged marriage due to their families' animosity towards each other.

title: The Moldau
summary: Vltava (The Moldau) is a symphonic poem by Bedřich Smetana, composed in 1874-75. It depicts the Vltava River flowing through the city of Prague and into the surrounding countryside. The piece is divided into nine sections, each evoking a different mood or scene: sunrise over the river, the river's flow, the river's wildness, the river's calm, the river's song, the river's joy, the river's sadness, the river's farewell, and finally its merging with the Danube.

title: "Papillons"
summary: Papillons (Butterflies) is a set of 12 piano pieces by Robert Schumann, composed in 1831. The work is characterized by its delicate and intricate melodies.

title: "Carnaval"
summary: Carnaval, Op. 9 (in German: Karneval), is a piano suite by Robert Schumann. The work was composed in 1834-1835 and first published in 1840-41. It consists of twenty-two pieces that reflect the moods of carnival, with each piece representing a different character or emotion.

title: Hungarian Dance No. 5
summary: The Hungarian Dances are a set of ten pieces for orchestra, WoO 1, composed by Johannes Brahms between 1866 and 1880. Hungarian Dance No. 5 in F-sharp minor is one of the most popular pieces from this set, known for its lively and energetic rhythm.

title: Waltz in A-flat major (Op. 39, No. 15)
summary: The Waltz in A-flat major is a waltz for piano written by Johannes Brahms. It is the 15th of his 25 waltzes, published as Opus 39.

title: "Orestes"
summary: The Orestes, Op. 93, is a choral oratorio in five movements by Felix Mendelssohn, based on the ancient Greek legend of the House of Atreus. The text was written by Robert Pippin, based on Homer's Iliad and Odyssey. The work is considered one of Mendelssohn's masterpieces.

title: "Hebrides Overture"
summary: A symphonic overture that showcases the musical genius of Felix Mendelssohn, inspired by his experience visiting the Hebrides. The piece is a reflection of the composer's poetic imagination and captures the beauty and ruggedness of the Scottish landscape.

title: An American in Paris
summary: An American in Paris is a ballet by George Balanchine, with music by George Gershwin. It was composed specifically for the Ballets Russes, and premiered on April 12, 1928, at the Théâtre du Champs-Élysées in Paris. The work is set to five movements of Gershwin's own orchestral composition, An American in Paris.

title: Rhapsody in Blue
summary: A fusion of classical and jazz music, Rhapsody in Blue is a famous orchestral composition written for piano and jazz band. The piece is characterized by its complex rhythms, harmonies, and melodies, blending the classical tradition with American jazz idioms.

title: Something's Coming
summary: Something's Coming is a song from the 1957 musical West Side Story, written by Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim. The song is sung by Tony, the male lead, as he awaits his first kiss with Maria, the female lead. It's a romantic ballad that explores the emotions of anticipation and nervousness.

title: Tonight
summary: The song 'Tonight' is a famous duet from the classic musical 'West Side Story'. It is sung by Tony and Maria, expressing their love for each other and their desire to be together. The lyrics capture the emotions of first love and the uncertainty of the future.

title: Adagio for Strings
summary: The Adagio for Strings, Op. 11, is a movement from Samuel Barber's String Quartet, composed in 1936. It was originally intended to be the final movement of his String Quartet but has since been performed as a standalone work. The piece is a tribute to those who lost their lives during World War II and is considered one of Barber's most well-known and enduring compositions.

title: Knoxville: Summer of 1915
summary: The Knoxville: Summer of '1915' is a symphonic poem by Samuel Barber, commissioned for the bicentennial of Thomas Hart Benton's birth. The work was premiered in 1948 and has since become one of Barber's most famous compositions. The piece evokes the nostalgic atmosphere of summer in East Tennessee, with vivid descriptions of nature, people, and events from that time period.

title: Fanfare for the Common Man
summary: Fanfare for the Common Man is a musical composition by American composer Aaron Copland, written in 1942. It was originally written as an introduction to the opening of Lincoln's Birthday concert on November 12, 1942. The piece features three main themes, which are presented successively: 'Farfan', 'Common Man', and 'Hymn'. The 'Common Man' theme is based on a folk tune from Vermont.

title: Appalachian Spring: Variations on a Shaker Melody
summary: A symphonic suite based on an earlier piece, Appalachian Spring is a celebration of American folk music. The work features four movements: Prelude, Danza, Variation III, and Finale.

title: Façade Suite
summary: The Façade Suites are two musical compositions by William Walton, based on the poetry of Edith Sitwell. The first suite was premiered in 1939 and is a setting of 11 poems from the collection Façade, with a narrator and a large orchestra. It is a modernist work that uses jazz rhythms and instrumentation to create a dramatic and expressive sound.

title: Portsmouth Point
summary: The Portsmouth Point Overture was composed by William Walton in 1926, inspired by a trip to Portsmouth. The overture is a depiction of the bustling harbor and life at sea. It has been featured in various films, including 'Henry V' (1944) and 'Zulu' (1964).

title: "Hymn to St Cecilia"
summary: The 'Hymn to St Cecilia' is a choral work for solo soprano, chorus, and orchestra composed by Benjamin Britten in 1942. It is a setting of the text by W.H. Auden and is considered one of Britten's most popular works.

title: "A Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra" - Theme from The Goon Show
alternative_title: A Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra - Theme from The Goon Show
summary: This is an adaptation of Benjamin Britten's 'Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra', with an added theme from the popular British radio comedy show, The Goon Show. It is a light-hearted and playful arrangement of the original piece.

title: Nimrod
summary: Nimrod is a musical composition by Edward Elgar, part of his Enigma Variations. It was written in 1899 and features a beautiful melody with a soaring violin solo.

title: Pomp and Circumstance March No. 1
summary: The 'Pomp and Circumstance' marches are a set of five military marches written by Edward Elgar between 1901 and 1930. The first march, in D major, is the most well-known and is often performed at coronations and other state events. It has been used as the theme music for the BBC since 1926.

title: The Lark Ascending
summary: The Lark Ascending, also known as The Lark Rising, is a piece for violin and orchestra by Ralph Vaughan Williams. It is one of his most popular works and is considered one of the greatest pieces in the repertoire for solo violin and orchestra. The piece was written in 1914, just before the start of World War I, and is a tribute to the beauty of nature and the joy of life.

title: Sea Symphony
summary: A Sea Symphony is a choral symphony by Ralph Vaughan Williams, composed between 1903 and 1909. The work was commissioned by the Liverpool Philharmonic Society to commemorate the opening of their new concert hall.

title: The Pines of Rome
summary: The Pines of Rome is a three-movement symphonic poem by Italian composer Ottorino Respighi, evoking the beauty and grandeur of the city's ancient ruins. Commissioned by Mussolini to celebrate the Fascist regime's conquest of Ethiopia in 1936, but written much earlier, this work is renowned for its vivid depiction of Rome's iconic landmarks.

title: The Fountains of Rome
summary: The Fountains of Rome is a symphonic poem by Ottorino Respighi, first performed in 1927. It's the first of three works that form his trilogy known as The Roman Triptych. The piece represents the history and grandeur of Rome through music, evoking scenes from ancient Rome.

title: Peter and the Wolf
summary: A musical composition designed for children, telling the story of Peter and his animal friends. The work features a narrator to describe the characters and their actions, while different instruments represent each animal. The piece is structured as a narrative with various instrumental interludes.

title: Romeo and Juliet: Dance of the Capulets
summary: The 'Dance of the Capulets' is a famous orchestral piece from Sergei Prokofiev's ballet 'Romeo and Juliet'. It is a lively, energetic movement that sets the tone for the rest of the ballet. The music is characterised by its quick, staccato rhythms and bold, dramatic melodies.

title: Bolero
summary: Bolero is a famous orchestral work composed by Maurice Ravel. It begins with a simple melody played by the flute, accompanied by a repetitive rhythmic pattern on the timpani. As the piece progresses, additional instruments join in, each playing the same melody in harmony. The work builds up to a dramatic and intense climax before resolving quietly.

title: Pavane pour une infante défunte
summary: The Pavane pour une infante défunte (Pavane for a Dead Princess) is a famous composition by Maurice Ravel, composed in 1899. It is a slow and mournful piece of music, written in a traditional pavane style. The work was composed as an orchestral piece but later arranged for piano solo. It has been widely performed and recorded.

title: Danse Macabre
summary: A tone poem that represents a night scene, in which Death personified as a woman is depicted dancing with skeletons. The piece begins with an eerie introduction of the clarinet, portraying Death as a mysterious and ominous figure. As the piece progresses, it becomes more lively and playful, featuring various musical themes to represent different aspects of life and death.

title: Carnival of the Animals: Finale
summary: The finale of Camille Saint-Saens' Carnival of the Animals, a suite for orchestra and narrator, features a grandioso conclusion with all the instruments playing together in a lively and celebratory manner. The piece is meant to evoke the final moments of a wild carnival, where everyone comes together to dance and celebrate.

title: Gymnopédie No. 1
summary: Gymnopédie No. 1 is a famous solo piano piece composed by Erik Satie in 1888. It is the first of three Gymnopédies, and its soothing melody has captivated audiences for generations.

title: Gnossienne No. 1
summary: Gnossiennes are a set of six piano pieces composed by Erik Satie in 1890. The Gnossienne No. 1 is the first piece in this set, characterized by its dreamy and contemplative atmosphere. The title 'Gnossienne' refers to the Greek goddess Gnosis, which represents knowledge.

title: Sinfonia Semplice
summary: The Symphony in E flat major, also known as the 'Sinfonia semplice', is a symphony by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It was composed in 1845 and premiered in Stockholm that same year.

title: Elegie for solo violin and string orchestra
summary: The Elegy for solo violin and string orchestra is a beautiful and melancholic piece of music that showcases the technical skills of the violinist. It's a slow, contemplative work that evokes feelings of sadness and loss.

title: "Impromptu No. 4 in A-flat major"
summary: The Impromptus (German: 'Impromptus' or 'Mäßiges Tempo', Op. posth. 142) are a collection of eight short piano pieces by Franz Schubert, written in the period between 1826 and 1828, during his final years. They were published in 1868 by Robert Schumann, with whom they became very popular.

title: "Piano Trio No. 2 in E-flat major, Op. posth."
alternative_title: Piano Trio No. 2 in E-flat major, Op. posth.
summary: The Piano Trio No. 2 in E-flat major, Op. posth., D. 929 is a chamber music work by Franz Schubert. It was composed in the summer of 1827 and published posthumously. The trio consists of piano, violin, and cello.

title: Symphony No. 94
alternative_title: Symphony No. 94 in G major (Surprise Symphony)
summary: The Surprise Symphony is a symphony by Haydn in three movements, composed in 1791. It is named for the sudden, unexpected shift from calm to energetic that occurs in the final movement.

title: String Quartet Op. 76, No. 3 'Emperor'
alternative_title: String Quartet Op. 76, No. 3 in C major
summary: The String Quartet Op. 76, No. 3 is the third of six string quartets composed by Joseph Haydn in 1797. It is characterized by a C major key and features five movements.

title: William Tell Overture
summary: The William Tell Overture is a famous orchestral overture composed by Gioachino Rossini for his opera 'William Tell'. The piece is known for its iconic and energetic melodies, and has been used in numerous films, TV shows, and other media. It is a popular example of early Romantic-era classical music.

title: The Barber of Seville: Overture
summary: The Barber of Seville is an opera buffa in two acts by Gioachino Rossini. The overture, also known as the Overture to Il Barbiere di Siviglia, is a famous and recognizable piece of classical music. It sets the tone for the comedic story of Figaro, a clever barber who helps his master win the heart of the beautiful Rosina.

title: "Symphonie Fantastique"
summary: The Symphonie Fantastique is a program symphony written by Hector Berlioz. It is considered one of the greatest compositions in classical music and a pioneering work in the genre of orchestral music.

title: "Les Nuits d'Été"
summary: Les Nuits d'Été (The Summer Nights) is a symphonic poem for solo voice and orchestra, set to six poems by Allan Cunningham. The work is known for its intense emotional expression, with the vocal part often describing scenes of love, nature, and death.

title: Asturias
summary: Asturias is a set of seven pieces for solo piano composed by Isaac Albéniz, Spanish composer. The piece is part of his suite 'España' and is considered one of the most technically demanding and beautiful pieces in classical music.

title: Granada
summary: Granada is a famous piece of music written by Spanish composer Isaac Albéniz in 1887. The piece, also known as 'Asturias', is part of the suite 'España' and is based on traditional Andalusian folk music from Granada. It's characterized by its beautiful, dreamy melody and complex piano arrangement.

title: Concierto de Aranjuez
summary: The Concierto de Aranjuez is a concerto for guitar and orchestra written by Joaquín Rodrigo in 1939. The work is structured into four movements, each evoking a different mood. It is considered one of the most popular and recognizable pieces of classical music today.

title: Tonadilla
summary: The Tonadilla, Op. 13, No. 1 is a piece for solo guitar composed by Joaquín Rodrigo in 1939-1940. It is a beautiful and expressive work that showcases the technical and emotional range of the guitar.

title: Adagio in G minor
summary: The Adagio in G minor for strings and organ, also known as the Second Adagio, is a musical composition by Tomaso Albinoni. It was originally published in 1707-1708, but it gained popularity in the late 20th century due to its use in the film Platoon.

title: Oboe Concerto in D minor, Op. 7 No. 6: Adagio
summary: The Oboe Concerto in D minor, Op. 7 No. 6 is a Baroque concerto for oboe and strings. Composed by Tomaso Albinoni, it is the sixth of his six oboe concertos published in 1700. The concerto is written in four movements: Adagio, Allegro, Largo, and Minuetto.

title: No Woman, No Cry
summary: A song about the struggles of life in Jamaica during the late 1960s and early 1970s. The lyrics describe the poverty and violence that plagued many communities, but also express a sense of hope and resilience.

title: Three Little Birds
summary: Three Little Birds is a song by Bob Marley and the Wailers from their album 'Exodus'. The lyrics are based on a traditional Jamaican folk song. In the song, Marley advises his listeners to live life in the present moment, and not worry about the future or past.

title: Misty Morning
summary: Misty Morning is a song by Peter Tosh, released in 1977 on his album 'Toussaint L'Ouverture'. The track features Tosh's soulful vocals and socially conscious lyrics, which explore themes of struggle and perseverance. With its laid-back rhythm and memorable melody, Misty Morning has become one of Tosh's most beloved songs.

title: Equal Rights
summary: A song about unity and equality for all people, regardless of their race or social status. It's a call to action to fight against oppression and strive for a better world.

title: Pressure Drop
summary: Pressure Drop is a song by Jamaican reggae band Toots and the Maytals. Released in 1969, it was one of the band's most popular songs and has since become a classic of the reggae genre. The song features Toots Hibbert's soulful vocals and a catchy horn section.

title: Monkey Man

title: L'Invitation au Voyage
summary: The poem 'L'invitation au voyage' by Baudelaire was set to music in 1891 by French composer Henri Duparc. The lyrics evoke a sense of longing and yearning for a distant and idyllic paradise, describing the beauty of nature and the allure of a luxurious and peaceful life.

title: Chanson Triste
summary: Also known as Lune d'automne, this is a setting of the poem of that name by Paul Verlaine. It was written for voice and piano. The text of the poem is one of the most beautiful examples of Verlaine's Symbolist poetry.

title: Prelude in C-sharp minor
summary: The Prelude in C-sharp minor, Op. 3, No. 2 is a famous piano piece by Sergei Rachmaninoff, composed when he was just 19 years old. It is part of his Opus 3 set of preludes and is considered one of the most technically challenging pieces for solo piano. The prelude is characterized by its dreamy, introspective quality, with a soaring melody that evokes a sense of longing.

title: Isle of the Dead
summary: The Isle of the Dead is a choral symphony by Sergei Rachmaninoff, inspired by an ancient Greek tomb near Athens. The work is characterized by its dark and contemplative mood, using somber tones to evoke feelings of mortality and melancholy. It's considered one of Rachmaninoff's most complex and emotionally charged works.

title: Piano Concerto No. 3
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 3 is a concerto for piano and orchestra, composed by Sergei Rachmaninoff in 1909. It was his final piano concerto and one of his most popular works. The concerto consists of three movements: Allegretto, Scherzo (Moderato), and Finale (Allegro). It requires great technical skill and musicality from the pianist.

title: Vespers, Op. 37: Konechnyi Bozheství
summary: The Vespers, Op. 37 is a choral work by Sergei Rachmaninoff, composed in 1915 for the Russian Orthodox Church. Konechnyi Bozheství, also known as Eternal Peace, is the final movement of the vespers. It's a serene and contemplative piece that reflects on eternal peace.

title: The Firebird
summary: The Firebird is a ballet composed by Igor Stravinsky between 1909 and 1910. The work was commissioned by the Ballets Russes, a Russian ballet company, and premiered in Paris on June 25, 1910. The score is based on Slavic folklore and fairy tales, particularly the legend of Prince Ivan and the Firebird.

title: Petrushka
summary: Petrushka, also known as The Burlesque on Themes from Act I and II of 'The Tale of Tsar Saltan', is a ballet score composed by Igor Stravinsky in 1910-11. It was originally intended to be the first part of a full-length ballet, but it became an independent work.

title: Pulcinella
summary: Pulcinella is a ballet score composed by Igor Stravinsky to libretto adapted from Giovanni Battista Pergolesi's opera 'La serva padrona'. The work was created for the Ballets Russes and premiered in Paris on May 15, 1920. It was the first major commission given to Stravinsky after his infamous 'The Rite of Spring' in 1913.

title: The Soldier's Tale
summary: The Soldier's Tale, also known as Histoire du soldat, is a ballet suite scored for soloists and orchestra. The work is based on the fairy tale of the same name by Hans Christian Andersen, in a Russian translation by Abram Yoffe. It tells the story of a soldier who makes a pact with the devil to gain wealth and power, but ultimately loses everything.

title: Capriccio Espagnol
summary: Capriccio espagnol, Op. 34, is a suite of pieces by Russian composer Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov based on Spanish themes. It was composed in 1887 and first performed in 1889.

title: Scheherazade - The Story of the King of Persia
summary: The Scheherazade suite is based on episodes from One Thousand and One Nights. It tells the story of a woman who is falsely accused of infidelity by her king husband, who orders his vizier to execute her. However, the vizier manages to save her life by telling the king that she will provide him with entertainment for one year in exchange for mercy.

title: Overture on Three Russian Themes
summary: The Overture on Three Russian Themes is a symphonic poem composed by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov. The work was written in 1886 and is based on three folk melodies from Russia. It is considered one of the composer's most popular works and showcases his mastery of orchestration.

title: May Night - Waltz
summary: May Night is an opera in four acts, with music by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov and a Russian libretto by Vladimir Belinski, based on Alexander Serov's 1849 novel of the same name. The work is considered one of Rimsky-Korsakov's most popular operas and has become a staple of the classical music repertoire.

title: Pictures at an Exhibition
summary: Modest Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition is a tone poem composed for solo piano. The work is a musical representation of a visit to an art exhibition, specifically the 'Exhibition of the Works by the Artists of the Leningrad Society of Watercolourists and Painters in Oil' held in St. Petersburg in 1874. Each movement of the piece is inspired by a specific artwork or painter. The music is descriptive and evocative, capturing the mood and atmosphere of each painting. With its beautiful melodies, contrasting dynamics, and rich harmonies, Pictures at An Exhibition has become one of Mussorgsky's most beloved works.

title: A Night on the Bare Mountain
summary: The piece, composed for a concert production of Nikolai Gogol's 'St. John's Eve', depicts a fantastical and nightmarish journey on Christmas Eve as the devil invites the damned to join him in revelry on Bald Mountain.

title: Gopak from Zhizn' za zhizn'
summary: The Gopak is a Ukrainian folk dance tune in the opera Zhizn' za zhizn' (Life for Life) by Modest Mussorgsky. It is one of his most popular and enduring compositions, and has been arranged and transcribed numerous times.

title: Bydło (The Oxen)
summary: Bydlo is a piece of music for large orchestra, composed by Modest Mussorgsky in 1876. The title refers to the Russian word for "oxen," and the music depicts a peasant cart being pulled through the streets, accompanied by folk melodies played on traditional instruments.

title: Symphony No. 9
summary: The Symphony No. 9 in E minor, Op. 95, B. 178, also known as From the New World, is a symphony written by Antonín Dvořák in 1893

title: Dumka
summary: Dumka is a piece for solo piano by Antonín Dvořák, composed in 1895. It is a folk-inspired melody with a simple and catchy structure, characterized by a lively rhythm and a sense of joy and playfulness.

title: Largo
summary: The Largo is the slow movement of Antonín Dvořák's Symphony No. 9 in E minor, Op. 95, also known as From the New World. It is one of the most famous and recognizable pieces of classical music, with a hauntingly beautiful melody that evokes the spirit of the American wilderness.

title: Rusalka - Song to the Moon
summary: Rusalka is an opera in three acts by Antonín Dvořák. The story is based on a Czech fairy tale and follows the fate of Rusalka, a water nymph who falls in love with a prince.

title: Slavonic Dance No. 8
alternative_title: Slavonic Dance No. 8 in G minor Op. 46
summary: The Slavonic Dances are a set of ten dances written by Antonín Dvořák between 1877 and 1886. The No. 8 in G minor, Op. 46 is part of this collection and features a lively rhythm with a mix of staccato and legato passages. It is characterized by its dramatic contrast between the opening melody and the subsequent virtuosic violin solo.

title: The Bartered Bride (Overture)
summary: The Bartered Bride is an opera by Bedřich Smetana, composed between 1863 and 1866. The overture is a lively and energetic piece that sets the tone for the rest of the opera. It features a mix of folk-like melodies and Classical-style orchestration.

title: Má Vlast
summary: Má vlast (My Homeland) is a symphonic poem by Bedřich Smetana, composed in 1874-79. It is a musical expression of the composer's love for his native Bohemia and its people. The work consists of six movements, each evoking a different region of Bohemia. The final movement, 'Šárka', tells the story of a Czech heroine who fights against the German invaders.

title: The Secret
summary: The Secret (or Tajný) is a symphonic poem by Czech composer Bedřich Smetana, written in 1863. The piece depicts the myth of Libuše, the legendary founder of Prague. It is part of Smetana's Má vlast suite and is considered one of his most famous works.

title: From the Península
summary: The 'Vltava' (also known as 'Má Vlast', which means 'My Country'), Op. 26, is a symphonic poem composed by Bedřich Smetana between 1874 and 1879. The work is divided into seven sections and features five different tempos.

title: Papillons
summary: Papillons (Butterflies) is a set of 12 piano pieces, Op. 2, composed by Robert Schumann in 1831. The piece is characterized by a lively and playful mood, with intricate fingerwork and a sense of whimsy.

title: Waldszenen
summary: Waldszenen, Op. 82 is a set of 14 short pieces for solo piano by Robert Schumann. It was composed in 1849 and first published posthumously in 1870. The work consists of two sections: the first seven pieces depict scenes of nature, including sunrise, noon, and sunset; the second seven pieces evoke emotions such as joy, sorrow, and longing.

title: Dichterliebe
summary: Dichterliebe (Poet's Love) is a song cycle for solo voice and piano, composed by Robert Schumann in 1840. It sets to music poems by Heinrich Heine, exploring themes of love, loss, and longing. The cycle consists of 20 songs, each capturing a unique emotional landscape.

title: Piano Quintet
summary: The Piano Quintet in E-flat major, Op. 44, is a chamber music composition by Robert Schumann, composed for piano and string quartet. The work consists of four movements: Allegro ma non troppo, Scherzo (Molto vivace), Largo, and Finale (Allegro molto). It is considered one of the most important works in the repertoire for chamber ensemble.

title: Waltz in A-flat major
summary: The Waltz in A-flat major, Op. 39, No. 15 is a waltz by Johannes Brahms, composed in 1865. It is one of his six published sets of eight short waltzes for piano, dedicated to his friend and fellow composer, Albert Dietrich.

title: Lullaby
summary: The Lullaby, also known as Wiegenlied (German for 'lullaby'), is a musical composition by Johannes Brahms. It was composed in 1868 and published posthumously in 1930. The piece is scored for solo piano and features a soothing melody that is intended to be calming and peaceful. The Lullaby is considered one of the most famous and beloved works of Brahms, and it continues to be popular among music lovers today.

title: Rhapsody in G minor
summary: The Rhapsody in G minor, also known as the G minor Rhapsody or simply Rhapsody, is a rhapsody for solo piano composed by Johannes Brahms. It was written in 1879 and dedicated to Hans von Bulow. The work is considered one of the most technically demanding pieces of piano music ever written. The piece has three themes: the first theme is announced at the beginning, the second theme is introduced after a dramatic episode, and the third theme provides a calm contrast.

title: Hungarian Dance No. 1
summary: One of a set of 21 Hungarian Dances, Op. 1, written by Johannes Brahms in the late 19th century.

title: Hebrides Overture
summary: The Hebrides Overture, also known as Fingal's Cave, is a symphonic poem written by Felix Mendelssohn in 1830. The piece was inspired by the Scottish composer Robert Burns' poem 'Fingal', which described the Hebrides Islands. The music is meant to evoke the mood and atmosphere of these islands. It begins with a gentle melody reminiscent of the sea, followed by a dramatic outburst, and eventually returns to the calm and peaceful theme.

title: Calm Sea and Prosperous Voyage
summary: The song 'Calm Sea and Prosperous Voyage' is a famous overture composed by Felix Mendelssohn. It was written in 1828-1830 for a Shakespeare play called 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'. The overture describes the journey of the characters from the beginning of the play, evoking a sense of calmness and serenity. The music is characterized by soothing melodies and harmonies that create a peaceful atmosphere.

title: Symphony No. 4 "Italian"
summary: The Italian Symphony, composed by Felix Mendelssohn in 1830-33, is a symphony that takes the listener on a musical journey through Italy. The symphony's four movements evoke the grandeur of Rome and the beauty of Venice, with vivid descriptions of the country's landscapes, art and culture.

title: Song Without Words: Book VI, D major (Op. 67/6)
summary: The Song Without Words is a set of six piano pieces composed by Felix Mendelssohn. Each piece has its own unique character and mood, with this sixth movement being in D major.

title: Elijah Op. 70
summary: The Elijah Op. 70, subtitled The Prophet, is a German oratorio composed by Felix Mendelssohn in the years 1849-50. It premiered on December 16, 1852, in Birmingham, England. The work tells the story of the Old Testament prophet Elijah, who calls down fire from heaven to consume the sacrifice offered by the priests of Baal and ultimately brings God's message of redemption.

title: I Got Rhythm
summary: I Got Rhythm is a popular song written by George and Ira Gershwin for the 1930 musical Girl Crazy. The song's melody was written by George, with lyrics by Ira.

title: My Man's Gone Now
summary: The song 'My Man's Gone Now' from the musical Porgy and Bess is a lament by the character Bess after her lover, Porgy, leaves. She sings about how she can't cope with life without him. The lyrics are heartfelt and poignant, conveying the pain of loss.

title: West Side Story Suite
summary: The West Side Story Suite is a symphonic adaptation of the iconic musical's score, arranged by Leonard Bernstein. It features many of the show's most recognizable melodies and themes, reimagined for an orchestral setting.

title: Candide Overture
summary: The Candide Overture is a concert piece composed by Leonard Bernstein in 1956. The music was written to celebrate the revival of Leonard Bernstein's operetta Candide, which opened on December 1, 1956. The overture is meant to be an instrumental representation of the themes and motifs that appear throughout the opera. It has become one of Bernstein's most popular and well-known works outside his musical theatre compositions.

title: Symphonic Dances from West Side Story
summary: The Symphonic Dances from Leonard Bernstein's West Side Story is a orchestral suite that takes the most iconic themes from the classic musical and presents them in a new, symphonic light. The work is a testament to Bernstein's skill as a composer and arranger, weaving together the jazz influences of the original score with classical instruments to create something entirely new.

title: Mambo: Dancer's Life
summary: The Mambo: Dancer's Life is a movement from Leonard Bernstein's Dance Suite, written in 1941. It is characterized by a lively and energetic rhythm, reflecting the spirit of dance.

title: Chichester Psalms
summary: The Chichester Psalms are a choral composition by Leonard Bernstein, setting the traditional Hebrew texts of the psalms for choir and orchestra. The work was premiered in 1965 at the Festival of St. Mary's Church in Chichester Cathedral, England. The psalm texts were set to three movements: Psalm 85, Psalm 100, and Psalm 131.

title: Medea's Meditation and Dance of Vengeance
summary: Medea's Meditation and Dance of Vengeance is a musical composition by Samuel Barber, written in 1947. The piece is part of the opera 'Medea', which is based on the ancient Greek tragedy by Euripides. It's a representation of Medea's inner turmoil and her meditation on revenge. The music is characterized by complex rhythms, dissonant harmonies, and a sense of anxiety.

title: Piano Concerto
summary: The Piano Concerto by Samuel Barber is a concerto for piano and orchestra, first performed in 1949. The work was commissioned by the American pianist Leon Fleisher, who premiered it with the New York Philharmonic under the baton of Dmitri Mitropoulos.

title: Violin Concerto
summary: The Violin Concerto by Samuel Barber is a concerto for solo violin and orchestra, composed in 1939. It was premiered on January 14, 1943, with the Philadelphia Orchestra, conducted by Eugene Ormandy, featuring the soloist, Jascha Heifetz. The concerto has three movements: Allegro, Adagio, and Presto.

title: Appalachian Spring
summary: A string quartet piece composed by Aaron Copland, scored for the Martha Graham Dance Company. It was premiered in 1944 and is considered one of the most iconic works of American classical music. The piece is characterized by a soaring melody, intricate rhythms, and an overall sense of American folk spirit.

title: Danse Macabre
alternative_title: Danse Macabre (A Symphonic Picture of Chopin's Fantasie)
summary: Danse macabre is a symphonic work by Aaron Copland, composed in 1940. The piece is based on the famous violin waltz from Frédéric Chopin's Fantaisie-Impromptu in C-sharp minor (Op. posth. 66). Danse Macabre uses the melodies and harmonies of the original work but transcribes them for orchestra, using a more dramatic and narrative approach.

title: Rodeo: Four Dance Episodes
summary: The Rodeo is a work for orchestra composed by Aaron Copland in 1942, one of his most famous compositions. It is based on four episodes from the life of cowboys: Buckaroo Holiday, Corral Nocturne, Saturday Night Ride, and Hoe-Down. The piece is known for its energetic rhythms and American folk music influences.

title: Cello Concerto
summary: The Cello Concerto in B minor for solo cello and orchestra is a concerto written by William Walton. The work was commissioned by the cellist Mstislav Rostropovich, who gave its first performance on April 26, 1956. The concerto is known for its dramatic and technically challenging parts, with some critics considering it one of the most important and demanding pieces in the cello repertoire.

title: Belshazzar's Feast
summary: A choral work in two parts, based on the Book of Daniel from the Old Testament. It tells the story of Belshazzar's feast, where the Babylonians use sacred vessels to drink wine and are subsequently defeated by the Persians.

title: Henry V Suite
summary: The Henry V Suite was composed by William Walton for the 1944 film 'Henry V', directed by Laurence Olivier. The suite is a collection of six movements, each highlighting a different aspect of the film's score. It is considered one of Walton's most famous works and has become a classic in the world of classical music.

title: Scapino
summary: Scapino, a ballet score by William Walton, tells the story of Scapin, a cunning servant in Moliere's comedy. The music is known for its wit and humor, capturing the character's quick thinking and clever antics.

title: Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra
alternative_title: The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra
summary: A musical composition written by Benjamin Britten in 1945, commissioned by Henry Wood for the Promenade Concerts. The work is a guide to the different instruments of the orchestra and their various sounds.

title: Four Sea Interludes
summary: The Four Sea Interludes are a set of four orchestral movements, each depicting a different aspect of the sea, as depicted in Benjamin Britten's opera Peter Grimes. The interludes are meant to evoke the moods and emotions of the sea and its effect on the characters in the opera.

title: The Young Pretender
summary: The Young Pretender is a song written by Benjamin Britten in 1946. The song is a tribute to Charles Edward Stuart, also known as Bonnie Prince Charlie. It is part of the musical 'Paul Bunyan' and is characterized by its lilting melody and poetic lyrics.

title: Sinfonia da Requiem
alternative_title: Sinfonia da Requiem: Sinfonia Da Requiem
summary: A large-scale choral work that sets the text of the Dies Irae (Day of Wrath) to music, with a dramatic and emotional score.

title: Canticle III: Still Falls the Rain
summary: A setting of Arthur Cecil Pigou's poem, this work is part of Benjamin Britten's 'Five Canticles'. The third canticle describes a scene of rain falling in the desert, where a pilgrim encounters God. It is characterized by a slow and contemplative pace, evoking feelings of calm and serenity.

title: Salut d'Amour
summary: Salut d'amour (French for "Hello, Love") is a popular salon piece composed by Edward Elgar in 1889. It was originally written as a piano piece, but later arranged for violin and orchestra. The melody is a beautiful and sentimental waltz that has become one of the most recognizable and beloved pieces of classical music.

title: Enigma Variations: Variation IX - Nimrod
summary: Variation IX, also known as Nimrod, is the ninth of Edward Elgar's Enigma Variations. It was written in memory of Axford (a fellow composer and pianist) who died after a short illness. The piece has become one of the most popular pieces from the entire Enigma Variations.

title: Pomp and Circumstance March No. 4
summary: A classic military march written for the coronation of King Edward VII, with a strong and stately melody that evokes a sense of grandeur and ceremony. The march is known for its energetic and celebratory feel, with a memorable theme that has become iconic in British culture.

title: English Folk Song Suite
summary: The English Folk Song Suite was written in 1934 by Ralph Vaughan Williams, and is a collection of six folk tunes, each representing a different region of England. The suite is a celebration of traditional English music, with themes ranging from nostalgic to majestic.

title: Job: A Masque for Dancing
summary: Job: A Masque for Dancing is a ballet score composed by Ralph Vaughan Williams in 1930. The work was commissioned to celebrate the coronation of King George V's daughter, Princess Mary. It premiered on October 29, 1931, at the Birmingham Hippodrome and has since become one of Vaughan Williams' most popular works. The score is characterized by its use of folk-inspired melodies and modal harmony.

title: The Wasps Overture
summary: The Wasps Overture is a piece for orchestra by Ralph Vaughan Williams, based on music from his opera The Wasps. It was first performed in 1909 and is one of the most popular pieces of British classical music. The overture is characterized by its lively and energetic melody, which captures the spirit of English summertime.

title: Fountains of Rome
summary: The Fountains of Rome is a symphonic poem in three movements composed by Ottorino Respighi. The work is inspired by the history and mythology of ancient Rome, with each movement evoking a different aspect of the city's past.

title: Ancient Airs and Dances
summary: The Ancient Airs and Dances is a set of three suites for string orchestra composed by Ottorino Respighi, inspired by Italian Renaissance music. The pieces are meant to evoke the feeling of ancient dances from the past.

title: La Boutique Fantasque
summary: La Boutique Fantasque (The Fantastic Shop) is a suite of music for piano, composed by Ottorino Respighi in 1919. The piece is a depiction of a shop where musical instruments are being sold, and each movement evokes the sounds of different instruments. It is considered one of Respighi's most popular and enduring works.

title: Piano Concerto No. 3
alternative_title: Piano Concerto No. 3 in C Major, Op. 26
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 3 is a concerto for piano and orchestra composed by Sergei Prokofiev between 1917 and 1921. It was the first of his concertos to be widely performed in the Soviet Union, which gave it significant currency during the years of Stalin's rule.

title: Symphony No. 5
summary: The Symphony No. 5 in B-flat major, Op. 100 is a symphonic work by Sergei Prokofiev written from 1937 to 1944 and first performed at the premiere of the ballet Romeo and Juliet on November 20, 1940. It was written for the Leningrad Philharmonic Orchestra, but its initial reception was lukewarm due to the difficulties in performance that made it less than ideal for a Soviet audience.

title: Lieutenant Kijé Suite
summary: The Lieutenant Kijé Suite is a suite for orchestra composed by Sergei Prokofiev in 1940. It was written to music used in the 1933 film Lieutenant Kijé, based on a novella by Leonid Solovyov. The suite is in four movements and features a combination of military fanfares, waltz rhythms, and lyric themes.

title: Piano Concerto in D major
summary: The Piano Concerto in D major is a concerto for piano and orchestra written by Maurice Ravel between 1929-1930. The work was commissioned by the Boston Symphony Orchestra, and it premiered on January 15, 1932, with the composer as soloist. The concerto consists of three movements: Allegro, Adagio assai, and Allegretto. It is considered one of Ravel's most technically demanding works for piano.

title: Pavane pour une infante defunte
summary: A beautiful and melancholic piece for solo piano, written in memory of a young girl who died in childhood. The pavane is a slow, stately dance that was popular in the 16th century, but Ravel's composition has become one of his most beloved works.

title: Miroirs: Noctuelles
summary: The piece is characterized by a dreamy, evocative quality, with soaring arpeggios and a sense of longing. It's one of Ravel's most beloved works for solo piano.

title: Gaspard de la nuit: Ondine
summary: The third movement of Gaspard de la nuit is titled 'Ondine' after a poem by Gautier, and features an evocative piano melody that captures the essence of the mythological water nymph. Ravel uses advanced techniques such as chromaticism and polyrhythms to create a sense of tension and release.

title: The Swan (from Carnival of the Animals)
summary: The Swan is a famous piece from Camille Saint-Saëns' 'Carnival of the Animals'. It's a beautiful and melancholic melody played by cello. The Swan is often used in films, TV shows, and commercials to evoke a sense of nostalgia and longing.

title: Symphony No. 3 "Organ"
summary: The Symphony No. 3 in C minor, Op. 78 'Organ' is a symphonic poem written by Camille Saint-Saens between 1885 and 1886. It was composed for the Exposition Universelle of 1889 in Paris, where it premiered on May 19, 1889.

title: Bacchanale
summary: The Bacchanale is a piece for orchestra, considered one of the most popular and recognizable works by Camille Saint-Saens. It was composed in 1887 as part of his opera 'Samson et Dalila'. The music depicts a wild dance, evoking ancient Roman festivals. It is known for its energetic and lively melody.

title: Gymnopédie No. 3
summary: The Gymnopédies are three piano pieces written by Erik Satie in the late 19th century, and published in 1888. They were originally intended to be performed by a chorus of men, singing a cappella, with the accompaniment of a piano or a string quartet. However, in the version that is most commonly played today, it is just the piano playing.

title: Sarabande Florale
summary: The Sarabande Florale (also known as Trois Gymnopédies, No. 1: Sarabande) is a piece of music composed by Erik Satie in 1887. It is part of his Trois Gymnopédies and is considered one of the most popular and enduring pieces of classical music.

title: Je Te Veux
summary: Je te veux (French pronunciation: [ʒət vø]) is a short piano piece by Erik Satie, composed in 1891. It has been described as 'one of the most beautiful and touching melodies ever written'. The piece features a simple but poignant melody played in a stately tempo, with a repetitive pattern of ascending chromatic arpeggios.

title: Sinfonia seria
summary: The Sinfonia seria in F minor is a symphony by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It was composed between 1847 and 1855, during which time Berwald was struggling with mental illness.

title: Sinfonia militare
summary: The Sinfonia Militare (Military Symphony) is a symphony written by Swedish composer Franz Berwald in 1840. The work was commissioned to commemorate the centenary of Gustav III's reign and is characterized by a sense of martial spirit and national pride.

title: Sinfonia concertante
summary: The Sinfonia concertante in F minor, Op. 10 is a work for strings by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It is one of the few orchestral works he composed and has been praised for its lyricism and technical ability.

title: Singing Lesson
summary: The Singing Lesson is a vocalises piece by Franz Berwald, written in 1848. It consists of three sections with different moods: a calm and dreamy introduction, an energetic and virtuosic middle section, and a final slow and introspective coda.

title: Elegy
summary: The Elegy in memory of Alicia Wennerstedt is a symphonic poem composed by Franz Berwald. It was written in 1855 as a tribute to his wife who had died the previous year. The piece is characterized by its mournful and melancholic tone, reflecting the composer's grief.

title: Ave Maria
summary: Ave Maria is a musical setting of the traditional Catholic prayer to the Virgin Mary, composed by Franz Schubert. The song is based on the melody of Bach's Cello Suite No. 1 and sets the Latin text of Walter Scott's poem 'The Lady of the Lake'.

title: Impromptu in A-flat major, Op. 142, No. 2
summary: The Impromptus on a theme by An die Musik are a set of four impromptus for solo piano, written in the summer of 1827. They were not published during Schubert's lifetime, but rather after his death by his friend and publisher Franz Sittner. The Impromptus are among Schubert's most popular works, and are considered some of the greatest pieces of piano music ever written.

title: Wanderer Fantasy, D. 760
summary: The Wanderer Fantasy, D. 760 is a piano piece written by Franz Schubert in 1822. It is one of his most famous and technically challenging works for solo piano. The piece is characterized by its dramatic and poetic qualities, with sudden changes in mood and tempo.

title: Piano Trio in E-flat major, D. 929: II. Andante con moto
summary: The Piano Trio in E-flat major, D. 929 is a chamber music composition by Franz Schubert. It consists of three movements and features a soothing and contemplative character in the second movement, 'Andante con moto'. This movement is characterized by a gentle melodic theme played by the violin, accompanied by a subtle dialogue between the piano and cello.

title: Unfinished Symphony
summary: The Unfinished Symphony, also known as Symphony No. 8 in B minor, D. 759, is a musical composition by Austrian composer Franz Schubert. It was composed in 1822 and left unfinished at the time of his death. The symphony consists of two movements: an Allegro moderato and an Andante con moto.

title: "Symphony No. 94"
summary: The Symphony No. 94 in G major, Hob. I:94, is a symphony by Joseph Haydn. It was written in 1790-91 and is one of the most famous of his symphonies. The work is known for its dramatic opening movement, which sets the tone for the rest of the symphony.

title: "Trumpet Concerto in E-flat major"
summary: The Trumpet Concerto in E-flat major is a concerto for trumpet and orchestra, composed by Franz Joseph Haydn. The concerto is written in three movements: Allegro, Adagio, and Rondo. The work is known for its virtuosic solo parts and its use of complex harmonies and counterpoint.

title: "Piano Sonata in C major (Hob.XVI:50)"
summary: The Piano Sonata in C major, Hob. XVI: 50, is a piano sonata by Franz Joseph Haydn. It was published in London in 1789 as part of the six-volume collection "Haydn's most esteemed musical compositions for the pianoforte".

title: "Symphony No. 104"

The song's lyrics are about drowning one's sorrows in drink after being stood up by a lover. Kurt Elling's version features his soulful vocals accompanied by a small group of musicians.

title: The Girl from Ipanema
summary: A cover of the classic Portuguese song 'Garota de Ipanema' (Portuguese for 'Girl from Ipanema') composed by Antonio Carlos Jobim and Vinicius de Moraes. The song was first recorded in 1964 by Stan Getz and Astrud Gilberto, but Kurt Elling's version is a smooth jazz take with lush orchestration and subtle nuances.

title: Samba de Orfeu
summary: Samba de Orfeu is a song by American jazz vocalist Kurt Elling, from his album 'The Messenger'. It has been interpreted as a reflection on the life of Orpheus in Greek mythology.

title: Lovers Turned Strangers

title: Come Sunday

title: Every Night

title: Just in Time

title: It's Easy to Remember

This a cappella piece showcases his vocal range, control, and emotion. The lyrics convey a sense of sincerity in relationships, where words are not needed to express love.

title: St. Louis Blues
summary: The St. Louis Blues is a famous blues song written by W.C. Handy in 1914, but this version is an a cappella arrangement performed by Bobby McFerrin. It's a beautiful and emotive rendition that showcases the singer's vocal range and expression.

title: Piano Concerto No. 4
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 4 in G major, Op. 58 is a concerto for piano and orchestra by Ludwig van Beethoven. It was composed in 1805 and premiered on March 22, 1807. The concerto consists of three movements: Allegro moderato, Adagio, and Rondo (Vivace).

title: Symphony No. 9 (Choral)
summary: Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 in D minor, Op. 125 is a choral symphony that sets the final movement of Friedrich Schiller's poem 'An die Freude' to music. The symphony is known for its heroic and celebratory tone, as well as its setting of Schiller's words in four languages: German, Latin, French, and English.

title: Appassionata
alternative_title: Piano Sonata No. 23 in F minor, Op. 57, 'Appassionata'
summary: The Piano Sonata No. 23 in F minor, Op. 57, known as the 'Appassionata', is a sonata for solo piano composed by Ludwig van Beethoven. It was written around 1804-05 and first published in 1807.

title: Waldstein Sonata
alternative_title: Piano Sonata No. 21 in C major, 'Waldstein', Op. 53
summary: The 'Waldstein' is a piano sonata written by Ludwig van Beethoven in 1803–04, one of his most technically demanding works. It consists of three movements: an introduction to the exposition of the first theme, an exposition of the second theme and a development section.

title: Violin Concerto
summary: The Violin Concerto in D major, Op. 61 is a concerto for solo violin and orchestra composed by Ludwig van Beethoven between 1806 and 1807. The work is known for its technical demands on the soloist and its rich, expressive melodies.

title: Requiem Mass in D minor
summary: The Requiem Mass in D minor, K. 626 is a musical composition by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. It was left unfinished at the time of his death and was completed by Franz Xaver Süssmayr. The work consists of six movements: Sequentia - Lacrimosa, Dies Irae, Rex tremendae, Offertorium - Domine Jesu Christe, Hostias et preces, Sanctus, Agnus Dei.

title: Symphony No. 40
summary: A symphony in G minor, written by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart in 1788. It is known for its dramatic and expressive qualities, with a slow introduction followed by three fast movements. The symphony has become one of the most famous works of classical music.

title: Don Giovanni Overture
summary: The Don Giovanni Overture, K. 527, is a symphonic overture composed by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart in 1787 to accompany his opera Don Giovanni. The overture is one of the most famous and influential classical music pieces ever written.

title: Horn Concerto No. 4
alternative_title: Horn Concerto No. 4 in E-flat major K. 495
summary: The Horn Concerto No. 4 in E-flat major, K. 495 is a concerto for horn and orchestra composed by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. It consists of three movements: Allegro maestoso, Andante cantabile, and Rondo (Allegro vivace).

title: Exsultate, Jubilate
summary: A virtuosic soprano aria from the 'Exultate, Jubilate' K. 165, composed by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart in 1772. The lyrics are from Psalm 118:24 and celebrate joy and gratitude towards God.

title: Magic Flute Overture
summary: The Magic Flute Overture, K. 620, is an overture written by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart for his final opera, The Magic Flute. It is considered one of the most popular and recognizable pieces of classical music.

title: Clarinet Concerto
alternative_title: Clarinet Concerto in A major K622
summary: The Clarinet Concerto in A major, K. 622, is a concerto for solo clarinet and orchestra by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. Composed in 1791, it was one of his last works and remains a popular piece among clarinetists and classical music fans.

title: Minuet in G
summary: The Minuet in G, BWV Anh. 114, is a minuet for solo harpsichord composed by Johann Sebastian Bach. It was likely written between 1707 and 1717. The minuet is characterized by its simple yet elegant melody and a strong rhythmic pulse. It is often performed at slow tempos, allowing the listener to appreciate the intricate details of the music.

title: Prelude in C Major
summary: The Prelude in C major, BWV 846, is a prelude for solo harpsichord by Johann Sebastian Bach. It was composed around 1703-1740 and published in the first part of The Well-Tempered Clavier. The prelude is characterized by a simple and elegant theme that evokes a sense of calmness and serenity. It's considered one of Bach's most popular and accessible compositions, often used in various contexts such as weddings, funerals, and meditation.

title: The Well-Tempered Clavier
summary: Composed for solo keyboard, The Well-Tempered Clavier is a collection of 48 preludes and fugues in all 24 major and minor keys. It's considered one of the most important and influential works in Western classical music.

title: Suite No. 3: Bourrée
summary: The Bourrée from Suite No. 3 in G minor, BWV 1004 is a short and lively dance movement that showcases the composer's mastery of counterpoint and ornamentation. The piece begins with a series of rapid arpeggios in both hands before introducing a simple but memorable melody. As the bourrée progresses, Bach employs a range of technical devices, including double stops, syncopation, and dramatic dynamic contrasts to create a sense of energy and tension.

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 2
alternative_title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 2 in F major, BWV 1047
summary: The Brandenburg Concerto No. 2 is the second of six concertos for orchestra that Johann Sebastian Bach composed in the early 18th century. It is a work of great musical beauty and technical skill, showcasing Bach's mastery of counterpoint and harmony. The concerto is scored for a large ensemble including two violins, three violas, one cello, one harpsichord, and continuo. It consists of three movements: Allegro, Adagio ma non tanto, and Allegro assai. The first movement features a lively and energetic theme played by the solo violin, while the second movement is a beautiful and melancholic slow dance. The third movement is a fast and virtuosic allegro that showcases the technical skill of the soloists.

title: Passacaglia and Fugue
alternative_title: Passacaglia and Fugue in C minor
summary: The Passacaglia and Fugue in C minor, BWV 582, is a musical composition by Johann Sebastian Bach. It is a passacaglia, a type of composition where a repeating bass line is varied with new counterpoint above it. The fugue section that follows the passacaglia has a complex and intricate structure. This piece is considered one of the most challenging and technically demanding pieces in the organ repertoire.

title: Spring
summary: The 'Spring' concerto is the first of four violin concertos in Antonio Vivaldi's famous collection 'The Four Seasons'. It's a lively and vibrant depiction of the joys of spring, with its bright melodies and dancing rhythms. The concerto is scored for solo violin, strings, and continuo, and it's divided into three movements: Allegro, Largo, and Allegro.

title: Winter
summary: The 'Winter' concerto from Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons', a set of four violin concertos that evoke the moods and scenes of each season. The 'Winter' concerto is written in the key of F minor, with a fast tempo and dramatic melody reflecting the cold, harsh weather of winter.

title: Summer
summary: The Four Seasons, Op. 8, No. 2 in G minor is a concerto for solo violin and orchestra composed by Antonio Vivaldi in the early 18th century. The piece is part of The Four Seasons set of concertos, a collection of four violin concertos that evoke scenes from nature throughout the changing seasons. Summer is one of the most well-known pieces from this work and features music that evokes feelings of joy, energy, and vitality.

title: Largo al Factotum
summary: Largo al factotum is a famous aria from the opera 'Il Barbiere di Siviglia' by Gioachino Rossini, not Antonio Vivaldi. title: Fugue in G minor for Organ

title: Gloria
summary: The Gloria in excelsis Deo (Glory to God in the highest) is a musical composition that begins with the Latin text of Luke 2:14. It was written by Antonio Vivaldi for his oratorio Gloria, RV 589, which sets parts of the New Testament, including Psalm 23 and the Magnificat, among other passages.

title: Il Cimento dell'Amor Misterioso
summary: The 'Il cimento dell'amor mio' (The Test of My Love) is a set of 12 violin concertos by Antonio Vivaldi. The work is also known as the 'L'estro armonico', which translates to 'Harmonic Inspiration'. This concerto, particularly the Largo part, is one of the most recognizable and beloved pieces from this collection.

title: Il Pianto della Madonna
summary: This cantata for solo voice and continuo is a poignant expression of sorrow and lamentation, with the Virgin Mary singing about her grief over the crucifixion of her son. The text is taken from a poem by Pietro Aretino.

title: Marche Slave
summary: Marche slave, also known as Slavonic March, is a musical work written by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky in 1876. It was composed to commemorate the anniversary of the Slavic people and is considered one of Tchaikovsky's most popular works.

title: String Quartet No. 13 in B-flat minor, Op. 130
summary: The String Quartets, Op. 110 and Op. 137 were written by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky in the autumn of 1893. The quartet in B-flat minor is one of six that make up his last chamber music works, composed when he was already ill. It is a melancholic work characterized by simplicity and grandeur.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1: Andante
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 1 in B-flat minor, Op. 23 is a concerto for piano and orchestra composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky in 1874-75. The work consists of three movements: Allegro con brio (fast and lively), Andante sostenuto (slow and sustained), and Allegro con fuoco (fast with fire).

title: Violin Concerto in D major, Op. 35: Finale
summary: The finale of the Violin Concerto is a virtuosic showpiece that has been a favorite among violinists and audiences alike for generations. It begins with a majestic statement by the soloist, which is answered by the orchestra in a soaring melody. The movement builds to a thrilling climax, featuring intricate fingerwork and sweeping arpeggios.

title: Eugene Onegin: Waltz
summary: The Waltz is a scene from the opera Eugene Onegin, in which Prince Gremin, a friend of Onegin's family, is hosting a party. The waltz is played as a grand ball, with many guests dancing and socializing. The music is lively and celebratory, capturing the sense of joy and abandon that comes with letting loose on the dance floor.

title: Prelude in D minor (Op. 28, No. 24)
summary: The Prelude in D minor is a piano piece composed by Frédéric Chopin as part of his 24 Preludes, Op. 28. It is known for its dramatic and expressive qualities. The prelude features a series of arpeggios that create a sense of tension, which is then released in the final section.

title: Waltz in D-flat major (Op. 64, No. 1)
summary: The Waltz in D-flat major is a piano waltz by Frédéric Chopin composed in 1847. It belongs to his Opus 64 collection, along with three other waltzes (also known as the 'L'heure du berger' or 'Shepherd's Hour'). This waltz was originally composed for solo piano and is characterized by a simple yet elegant melody.

title: Mazurka in C-sharp minor (Op. 30, No. 4)
summary: The Mazurka in C-sharp minor, Op. 30, No. 4 is a piano piece by Frédéric Chopin. It was composed in 1838-40 and is part of his Opus 30 set of mazurkas.

title: Funeral March (Sonata No. 2)
summary: The Funeral March in C minor, also known as the Marche Funebre, is a movement from Frédéric Chopin's Piano Sonata No. 2, published in 1840. The piece is characterized by its somber and mournful melody, often used to represent death or mourning.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 1 in E minor, Op. 11, is a concerto for piano and orchestra composed by Frédéric Chopin. The work was written between 1830 and 1835 when the composer was just 19-23 years old. It consists of three movements: Allegro maestoso, Romanze, and Rondo. Chopin's innovative approach to harmony and structure made this concerto a groundbreaking work in the classical repertoire.

title: Waltz in D-flat major (Op. 70, No. 3)
summary: The Waltz in D-flat major is a waltz for solo piano by Frédéric Chopin. It was composed in 1827 and published in 1832 as one of the López de Gomara waltzes, a collection of waltzes dedicated to Juan Crisostomo de Arrieta's patron, Marquía Óscar de Olabarria Lopez de Gomara.

title: Nocturne in C-sharp minor (Op. 27, No. 1)

title: Piano Sonata in B minor S. 178
summary: The Piano Sonata in B minor, also known as the 'Sonata in B minor for solo piano', is a sonata composed by Franz Liszt. It was written between 1852 and 1853 and was considered one of Liszt's most technically challenging compositions. The sonata consists of four movements: Maestoso, Agitato assai – Molto agitato, Largo, and Allegro.

title: Unstern! Eine Symphonie nach Goethe's Faust
summary: Unstern, which translates to 'bad luck' in German, is a symphonic poem by Franz Liszt, inspired by the character of Faust from Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's play. The piece depicts the supernatural forces that surround Faust and his ill-fated pursuit of knowledge and power.

title: Malagueña
summary: Malagueña is a piece of piano music based on Spanish folk melodies. It was composed by Franz Liszt in 1864 and dedicated to the Spanish composer Joaquín Verdaguer y Santamaría. The piece is known for its beauty, harmony and technical difficulty.

title: Mazeppa
summary: Mazeppa is a descriptive piano piece by Franz Liszt, written in 1834-35. It's a tribute to the Ukrainian Cossack leader Ivan Mazepa, who fought against the Russian Empire in the late 17th century. The piece is known for its virtuosic and expressive qualities, with complex rhythms and arpeggios that evoke the horseback ride of Mazeppa. The music is divided into several sections, each representing a different aspect of Mazeppa's life and struggles.

title: Mephisto Waltz No. 4
summary: The Mephisto Waltz is a musical composition by Franz Liszt, written in the form of a waltz. The work was composed in 1859-1860 and consists of nine movements. It is considered one of Liszt's most important compositions for piano.

title: Grande Fantaisie de Bruyères
summary: The Grande Fantaisie de Bruyères is a piano piece composed by Franz Liszt, based on themes from his opera Hamlet. The piece is characterized by its intense and dramatic music, featuring intricate arpeggios and chromatic passages.

title: Alcina: Ombra Mai Fu
summary: Ombra mai fu is a famous aria from George Frideric Handel's opera Alcina, composed in 1735.
