The music is a beautiful and poignant expression of Ruggiero's despair and heartache.

title: Rinaldo: Lascia Ch'io Pianga
summary: Aria from the opera Rinaldo, the music is serene and peaceful. The lyrics are about leaving someone alone so they can weep and lament. The singer asks to be left alone, it's a moment of melancholy, but also of acceptance.

title: Acis and Galatea: Where Shallow Fish More Blest
summary: Acis and Galatea is an opera by George Frideric Handel, written in 1718. The libretto is by Nicolas Brady and John Hughes. title: Giulio Cesare: V'adoro pupille
summary: V'adoro pupille is a aria from the opera Giulio Cesare by George Frideric Handel. The song is sung by Cleopatra and is one of the most famous arias in the opera. It is a expression of love and devotion to Julius Caesar, with whom she falls in love.

title: Messiah: Rejoice Greatly
summary: "Rejoice Greatly" is a chorus from George Frideric Handel's oratorio "Messiah." The text is taken from the Bible, specifically Isaiah 35:10. The piece is written in a joyful and lively style, with a strong emphasis on the vocal performance.

title: Almira: Ah! Crudel, come posso vivere
summary: Ah! Crudel, come posso vivere is an aria from George Frideric Handel's opera Almira. summary: The Messiah is an oratorio composed by George Frideric Handel on a libretto by Charles Jennens. It was first performed in Dublin, Ireland in 1742. The work is divided into three parts and features various musical numbers, including recitatives, arias, choruses, and instrumental movements.

title: Xerxes: Ombra Mai Fu
summary: From the opera 'Serse' (also known as Xerxes) by George Frideric Handel. This aria is a showcase for the vocal talents of the tenor, and is one of the most famous and beloved pieces in all of opera.

title: La Traviata: Sempre Libera
summary: Sempre libera (Always free) is a famous aria from Act 1 of Giuseppe Verdi's opera La Traviata. The song is sung by the character Violetta, who is trying to convince herself that she will always be free and independent.

title: Aida: Casta Diva
summary: Casta diva, from the opera Aida, is a famous aria sung by the title character. It's an expression of the princess Aida's inner turmoil and passion as she waits for her lover Radamès. The music captures her longing and love.

title: Rigoletto: Bella Figlia dell'Amore
summary: Duke's daughter Gilda has fallen in love with his trusted counselor, but he does not return her affections. She is killed by the Duke's henchmen, and the opera ends with the death of the Duke.

title: La Traviata: Overture

title: Aida: O terra addio
summary: The opera 'Aida' is a classic tale of love and betrayal, set in ancient Egypt. title: Nabucco: Va, pensiero
summary: Va, pensiero (Chorus of the Hebrew Slaves) is a famous chorus from Giuseppe Verdi's opera Nabucco. It is sung by the Jewish people who have been enslaved and are longing to be free. The lyrics describe their suffering and their hope for freedom.

title: La Traviata: Addio del passato
summary: In Act II of La Traviata, Violetta's aria 'Addio del passato' is a poignant farewell to her past life. As she prepares for her death from tuberculosis, she reflects on the sacrifices she made for love and the fleeting nature of human existence. The aria is a masterpiece of Verdian melody and expression, conveying the depth of Violetta's emotions through soaring vocal lines and heart-wrenching harmony.

title: Rigoletto: Questa o quella

title: I Lombardi alla prima crociata: In braccio alle spose loro
summary: I Lombardi alla Prima Crociata is an opera in five acts by Giuseppe Verdi. The opera premiered at the Teatro San Benedetto in Venice on February 11, 1843. title: Aida: Ombra mai fu
summary: Aria from the opera Aida, sung by the slave girl Amneris. She sings of her love for Radames, who is promised to marry Aida. The aria is a declaration of love, but also a recognition of the impossibility of their love.

title: Good Friday Song from Parsifal
summary: The Good Friday Music, also known as the Easter Oratorio, is a movement from Richard Wagner's opera Parsifal. It is a meditation on the crucifixion of Christ and is one of the most famous and revered moments in all of classical music.

title: Flower Song from Tristan und Isolde
summary: The Flower Song, also known as the 'Tristan's Farewell', is a famous aria from Richard Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde. title: Brannleider's Song from Der Ring des Nibelungen
summary: The Brunnhilde's song, also known as 'Erlönig', is a piece from Richard Wagner's opera Der Ring des Nibelungen. The song describes the feeling of being abandoned and left to die on a mountain.

title: Siegfried's Funeral March from Gotterdammerung
summary: The final movement of Richard Wagner's epic opera 'Götterdämmerung' (Twilight of the Gods) is a somber and mournful funeral march for Siegfried, the hero of the story. The music is a poignant reflection on the passing of greatness and the end of an era.

title: Pilgrims' Chorus from Tannhauser
summary: The Pilgrim's Chorus, also known as the 'Song of the Pilgrims', is a famous aria from Richard Wagner's opera Tannhäuser. The chorus is sung by the pilgrims who are returning from Rome and are seeking redemption for their sins.

title: Lohengrin's Entrance from Lohengring
summary: Lohengrin's Entrance from Lohengrin, also known as Act I Scene 1 no. 1, is a famous orchestral piece by Richard Wagner. The music describes the entrance of Lohengrin, a knight of the Holy Grail, into the hall of King Henry I of Germany. This moment marks the beginning of the opera and sets the tone for the rest of the story.

It is based on a Russian folk tale and features a fast-paced, intricate melody that has become synonymous with the bumblebee. The piece requires great technical skill to play due to its complex rhythms and fingerwork.

title: Sadko
summary: The symphonic poem 'Sadko' is based on a Russian folk tale. The story revolves around the life of Sadko, a fisherman who becomes wealthy after discovering a hidden treasure in the Sea of Azov. However, his wealth and fame do not bring him happiness, and he ultimately dies a tragic death.

title: Scheherazade
summary: The musical composition Scheherazade is a tone poem in four movements, based on the story from One Thousand and One Nights. It was composed by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov between 1887 and 1888 for the Russian Ballet company. The ballet premiered in St. Petersburg in 1888, with Marguerite Messiaen as Scheherazade.

title: Mlada
summary: The Mlada is a symphonic poem composed by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov in 1892. The work is based on Slavic mythology and features a complex structure of themes that reflect the story of a young woman named Mlada who falls in love with a mortal man, defying her father's wishes.

title: The Tsar's Bride: Overture
summary: The Tsar's Bride is an opera in four acts, composed by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov. The overture is a grand and majestic piece that sets the tone for the rest of the opera. It features a mix of Russian folk melodies and orchestral textures, creating a sense of drama and tension.

title: Mozart and Salieri
summary: A musical depiction of the rivalry between two famous composers, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and Antonio Salieri. The piece is scored for a large orchestra and features a series of contrasting episodes that evoke the different moods and emotions of the story. It includes dramatic passages, as well as more lyrical and introspective moments.

title: Oriental Dance
summary: The Oriental Suite, Op. 28 is a set of seven orchestral pieces composed by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov in 1899-1900. The suite was inspired by the composer's interest in Middle Eastern and Asian music.

title: A Moonlight Fantasy
summary: A Moonlight Fantasy is an orchestral suite that evokes the beauty and mystery of a moonlit night. It's a dreamy, enchanting piece with a soothing melody.

title: The Hut on Fenny Island
summary: The Hut on Fenny Island (also translated as 'A Village by the River Mere') is a piano piece composed by Modest Mussorgsky in 1873. The work was commissioned by Nadezhda von Meck, who was also a patron of Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky and Sergei Rachmaninoff.

title: Bydło (Cossack Theme)
summary: Bydło (Polish for 'cart') is a piece from the suite Mlada, composed by Modest Mussorgsky. The theme is based on a folk melody from Ukraine and depicts a Cossack's cart and horses.

title: Tuileries
summary: Tuileries, also known as The Tuileries Garden in the sun, is a movement from Modest Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition. It evokes the atmosphere of a sunny day in Paris, with children playing and birds singing.

title: Il Vecchio Castello
summary: The piece is a programmatic work based on an old, abandoned castle. The first section of the piece portrays the old castle and its history, with a range of moods from serene to tumultuous.

title: The Gnome
summary: The Gnome is a movement from Modest Mussorgsky's 'Pictures at an Exhibition' suite. The piece depicts the character of an old gnome who has been left behind and is now dying, surrounded by his belongings.

title: Baba Yaga
summary: Baba-Yaga is a symphonic poem composed by Modest Mussorgsky in 1869. The work was originally intended to be part of the collection 'Pictures at an Exhibition', but it was eventually removed and became a standalone piece. Baba-Yaga features a haunting, dreamlike melody inspired by Russian folklore, telling the story of a witch who lives in a hut that stands on chicken legs.

title: Samovar
summary: Samovar (Russian: Самовар) is a piano piece from Modest Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition. The track is named after the samovar, a traditional Russian tea urn. The piece is often performed as part of the larger work and is known for its lively and folk-inspired melody.

title: Slavonic Dances Op. 46
summary: The Slavonic Dances, composed by Antonín Dvořák in 1886 and revised in 1891, are a set of eight orchestral pieces, each based on traditional Czech folk melodies. The work is divided into two sets: Op. 46 (published in 1899) and Op. 72 (published posthumously in 1912).

title: Rusalka (Waltz of the Mermaids)
summary: The Rusalka is a waltz from Antonín Dvořák's opera of the same name. The waltz features beautiful melodies and a lively rhythm, evoking the image of mermaids in a mythical underwater world.

title: Cello Concerto in B minor
summary: The Cello Concerto in B minor, Op. 104 is a concerto for solo cello and orchestra written by Antonín Dvořák in 1895. The concerto consists of three movements: Allegro, Adagio ma non troppo, and Finale: Allegro moderato. It is considered one of the most technically demanding and emotionally challenging works for cellists. The concerto was composed during a period of great personal and professional change for Dvořák, who had recently returned to Prague after living in New York City.

title: Symphony No. 7
alternative_title: Symphony No. 7 in D minor Op. 70
summary: The Symphony No. 7 in D minor, Op. 70 is an orchestral symphony by the Czech composer Antonín Dvořák composed in 1884-85. The work was commissioned by the London-based impresario William Schwenck Gilbert and premiered on March 25, 1892 at the Queen's Hall, London.

title: String Quartet No. 12, "American"
summary: The String Quartet No. 12 is a chamber music composition by Antonin Dvorak, written in 1893 and dedicated to Robert Hausmann, a German viola player and member of the Joachim Quartet.

title: Humoresque
summary:
The Humoreske in B-flat minor, Op. 101, is a piece for solo piano composed by Antonín Dvořák in 1894. The title 'Humoreske' comes from the Czech word for "humor" or "amusement," and the work's lighthearted and playful character reflects this.

The piece consists of six variations on a recurring theme, with each variation showcasing a different aspect of the melody. Dvořák uses a range of musical techniques to create a sense of drama and tension, including sudden changes in dynamics and articulation. The Humoreske ends with a lively and energetic coda that recalls the opening theme.

title: Piano Quintet No. 2 in A major
summary: The Piano Quintet No. 2 in A major, Op. 81 is a work for piano and string quartet by Antonín Dvořák. It was composed in 1887 and is one of the composer's most famous works.

title: Song to the Moon
summary: The 'Song to the Moon' (Cesky: Vesela v lase noci) is a soprano aria from Act III of Antonin Dvoraks opera Rusalka. The lyrics are taken from an old Czech folk poem and tell of the longing and love of the wood nymph Rusalka for Prince Vladimir.

title: The Bartered Bride (Otec a syn)
summary: The Bartered Bride (Ceninka) is an opera by Bedřich Smetana. It tells the story of a young woman, Mařenka, who is betrothed to a man she does not love in order to maintain her family's fortune. The opera explores themes of love, loyalty, and social class.

title: Die Moldau
summary: The Moldau (Vltava) is a symphonic poem composed by Bedrich Smetana. The work depicts the course of Vltava River through the Czech landscape, from its source in the Bohemian Forest to its confluence with the Elbe River.

title: Richard III
summary: Richard III is a symphonic poem by Bedrich Smetana, written in 1857. The music was meant to accompany Shakespeare's play of the same name and reflects Smetana's vision of Richard III as a villainous and destructive figure.

title: The Two Widows
summary: The Two Widows (Czech: Dvě vdovy) is a symphonic poem by Bedřich Smetana, composed in 1874. It was originally intended to be the first movement of his larger work The Bartered Bride, but it was eventually published separately.

title: Prodaná nevěsta - Prolog
summary: The Bartered Bride is an opera in three acts, the third of Bedřich Smetana's 'Má vlast' cycle. The story revolves around a young woman, Marenka, who is betrothed to a wealthy nobleman, but falls in love with another man, Jeník. The opera is known for its beautiful music and comic scenes.

title: My Country, Thou Art Exquisite and Beautiful
summary: The final movement of Smetana's Má vlast symphonic poem is a poignant tribute to his homeland. The music reflects on the beauty and tragedy of Czech history, with a soaring melody that evokes a sense of longing.

title: Vltava
summary: Vltava, also known as Ma Vlast (My Homeland), is a symphonic poem by Bedřich Smetana. It is the second in his series of six compositions based on Czech landscapes and national themes. The work describes the river Moldau (Vltava) flowing through the Bohemian countryside.

title: Mladi chudák
summary: The song 'Mladý chudák' (The Young Beggar) is an opera by Bedřich Smetana. It was composed in 1868 and premiered the same year. The story revolves around a young beggar who is mistreated by society but ultimately finds acceptance.

title: Šárka
summary: The track Šárka is the last of Bedřich Smetana's six symphonic poems called Má vlast (My Fatherland). It premiered on February 17, 1882. The piece depicts the legendary Libuše, the daughter of Krok, who seeks to avenge her brother and sister-in-law. In the opera Šárka, composed in 1875-77, Libuše is one of the three sisters.

title: "Arabeske"
summary: The Arabeske in A major, Op. 18, is a set of 10 variations for solo piano composed by Robert Schumann. The piece is a showcase of technical virtuosity and expressive depth, with each variation exploring a different aspect of the original theme.

title: "Humoresque"
summary: The Humoreske in B-flat major, Op. 20, is a piano piece by Robert Schumann composed in 1839-1840. It is often performed as four movements, although it was originally intended to be played continuously. The work is characterized by its lively and playful mood, with intricate fingerwork and complex rhythms.

title: "Etudes Symphoniques"
summary: A set of 12 etudes for solo piano that showcase the composer's mastery of technical and expressive elements. Each piece is a musical miniature, evoking different moods and characters through complex harmonies and melodies.

title: "Dichterliebe"
summary: The cycle of songs 'Dichterliebe' is a set of 18 poems by Heinrich Heine, arranged to music by Robert Schumann. The cycle describes the poet's love for a woman who does not return his affections, and he is left heartbroken and dejected.

title: "Kreisleriana"
summary: A set of 8 pieces for solo piano, characterized by complex and expressive melodies. The title refers to the 17th-century German composer Johann Heinrich von Kreisler. Each piece is a representation of his style and technique, with a focus on lyricism and musicality.

title: "Fantasie in C major"
summary: The Fantasie in C major, Op. 17 is a set of three pieces for solo piano composed by Robert Schumann between 1838 and 1840. The work consists of an Allegro, Largo, and Allegretto, each representing the contrasting moods that Schumann aimed to convey.

title: "Symphony No. 1"
summary: The Symphony No. 1 in B-flat major, Op. 38, is a symphonic poem by Robert Schumann. It was composed between 1839 and 1840 and premiered on March 5, 1841. The symphony is divided into four movements: Vivace, Larghetto, Allegro, and the Finale.

title: Waltz in A-flat major, Op. 39, No. 15
summary: The Waltz in A-flat major, Op. 39, No. 15 is a waltz for piano by Johannes Brahms. It is the last of four waltzes composed by Brahms and published in 1865 as part of his Opus 39 collection. The piece is known for its lyricism and elegance, with a gentle swaying rhythm that creates a sense of tranquility.

title: Lullaby, WoO 59
summary: A lullaby composed by Johannes Brahms for his sister-in-law's baby. The piece is a gentle and soothing melody, often played on the piano or sung to children.

title: Hungarian Dance No. 7
summary: The Hungarian Dances are a series of 21 pieces for piano and orchestra, Op. 35, composed by Johannes Brahms between 1866 and 1868, and published in 1869. No. 7 is the most famous of all, with its lively rhythm and energetic melody. It was originally written as an orchestral piece but was later arranged for solo piano. The dance has a strong folk influence, reflecting the Hungarian culture and traditions.

title: Intermezzo in A major, Op. 118, No. 2
summary: The Intermezzo in A major, Op. 118, No. 2 is a short piano piece by Johannes Brahms. It is characterized by a soothing and calming melody, with a gentle and flowing rhythm.

title: Piano Trio No. 1 in B major, Op. 8 - Notturno
summary: The Piano Trio No. 1 in B major, Op. 8, is a chamber music composition by Johannes Brahms, written in 1854-55 when the composer was just 17 years old. The work consists of four movements: Allegro con spirito, Scherzo (Allgroscherz), Andante, and Notturno (Largo). The Notturno is a slow and peaceful movement that features a beautiful melody for the violin.

title: Violin Concerto in D major, Op. 77 - Adagio
summary: The Violin Concerto in D major, Op. 77 is a concerto for violin and orchestra composed by Johannes Brahms. It is considered one of his most technically demanding works, requiring the soloist to possess great virtuosity and technical skill. The Adagio movement is the second movement of the concerto and is known for its beautiful and expressive melody.

title: Rhapsody in G minor, Op. 79, No. 2
summary: The Rhapsody in G minor, Op. 79, No. 2 is a composition by Johannes Brahms for solo piano. It consists of three movements and is characterized by its expressive melodies and complex harmonies. The work is known for its emotional intensity and is considered one of the most technically challenging pieces in the classical repertoire.

title: Piano Quartet No. 3 in C major, Op. 60 - Allegretto
summary: The Piano Quartet No. 3 in C major, Op. 60 is a work for piano and string trio by Johannes Brahms. It was composed in 1874-75 and dedicated to his friend Joseph Joachim. The Allegretto movement is the third of four movements and features a gentle, lilting melody played by the violin, accompanied by a soothing piano accompaniment.

title: Symphony No. 3
summary: The third symphony by Felix Mendelssohn, written in 1841-42. It is a large-scale work consisting of four movements. The first movement is marked Allegro di molto and the second is Andante con moto.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 1 in G minor, Op. 25 is a concerto for piano and orchestra written by Felix Mendelssohn in 1822-23. It is one of the most popular and technically demanding concertos for solo piano and orchestra. The work consists of three movements: Allegro assai - Allegro di molto, Scherzo: Molto allegro e vivace, and Adagio.

title: Song Without Words Op. 30 No. 6
summary: The Song Without Words, Op. 30, No. 6 is a piece for solo piano composed by Felix Mendelssohn in 1842. It is the sixth of six movements from his Op. 30 collection. The piece features a lively and energetic melody with intricate fingerwork.

title: Scherzo and Allegro
summary: The Scherzo and Allegro in A minor, Op. 81 is a piano work by Felix Mendelssohn, composed in the summer of 1837 while he was on his honeymoon with Cécile Charoux.

title: Rondo Capriccioso
summary: A virtuosic violin solo piece that features a series of intricate and expressive passages. The work is characterized by its dramatic contrasts, from the slow, introspective Largo to the fast, energetic Allegro.

title: Violin Concerto
summary: The Violin Concerto in E minor, Op. 64 is a concerto for violin and orchestra composed by Felix Mendelssohn. It was written in 1838 and revised in 1844.

title: Lieder Ohne Worte (Song Without Words) Op. 19b No. 4
summary: A beautiful and soothing piece of music for solo piano, characterized by a gentle melody and subtle dynamics. The song is part of a collection called 'Songs Without Words' and features intricate fingerwork and expressive phrasing.

title: Overture to A Midsummer Night's Dream
summary: The Overture to A Midsummer Night's Dream is a classical music composition by Felix Mendelssohn, written in 1841 for the play of the same name. It is considered one of the most beautiful and evocative orchestral pieces ever written, capturing the magical atmosphere of Shakespeare's play.

title: Summertime
summary: Summertime is a song written by George Gershwin for his opera Porgy and Bess. The lyrics were written by DuBose Heyward, who also wrote the libretto for the opera. The song has become one of Gershwin's most popular works and is often performed as a standalone piece.

title: Lady Be Good
summary: A jazz composition by George Gershwin, 'Lady Be Good' is a popular and recognizable piece of music that has been featured in numerous films and stage productions. It's characterized by its catchy melody and syncopated rhythms.

title: The Man I Love
summary: The Man I Love is a popular song written by George Gershwin and Ira Gershwin. It was introduced in the Broadway musical Lady, Be Good!, and has since become one of the composer's most beloved songs. The lyrics describe a person who is willing to make sacrifices for their loved one.

title: Fascinating Rhythm
summary: Fascinatin' Rhythm is a song composed by George Gershwin, with lyrics written by Ira Gershwin. It was introduced in the musical 'Lady Be Good'. The song features a complex rhythm and a memorable melody that has made it a classic of American popular music.

title: Let's Call the Whole Thing Off
alternative_artist: George Gershwin (as part of a collaboration with Ira Gershwin and others)
summary: The song was written by George and Ira Gershwin in 1936, as part of the musical 'Shall We Dance'. It features a witty dialogue between two people debating whether they can continue their romance despite their differences. The lyrics are full of clever wordplay and banter, showcasing the Gershwins' skill with language.

title: They Can't Take That Away From Me
summary: A song composed by George Gershwin, with lyrics by Ira Gershwin. The song is a duet between the male and female lead vocals, reflecting on the memories of a past love affair. It was written for the Broadway musical 'Shall We Dance', and has since become one of Gershwin's most famous songs.

title: West Side Story Medley
summary: The West Side Story Medley is a medley of songs from the iconic musical West Side Story, composed by Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim. The medley includes 'Something's Coming', 'Maria', 'America', 'Tonight', 'Jet Song', and 'Gee, Officer Krupke'. This medley showcases the energetic and lively music of the original musical.

title: Somewhere
summary: From West Side Story, the song Somewhere is a ballad that conveys the longing for an ideal world where people live in harmony. It's a poignant expression of the hope for a better tomorrow, with lyrics that reflect on the beauty of such a world and the contrast to the reality of urban life.

title: I Could Write a Book
alternative_artist: Richard Rodgers & Lorenz Hart / arr. Leonard Bernstein
summary: I Could Write a Book is a popular song written by Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart in 1937, for the musical Babes in Arms. It has since been covered by many artists, including Ella Fitzgerald, Frank Sinatra, and Dean Martin. The song's lyrics describe the joy of finding the right person to love.

title: Fancy Free
summary: Fancy Free is a ballet in three movements, set to the music of Leonard Bernstein's score. The ballet premiered at the Metropolitan Opera House in New York City on April 24, 1947. It was choreographed by Jerome Robbins and danced by the Ballet Society.

title: Lincoln Center Preview - Fancy Free
summary: Fancy Free, also known as West Side Story Suite from the ballet, is a musical suite by Leonard Bernstein. The suite was composed in 1946-47 as the music for Jerome Robbins' ballet Fancy Free. It was originally performed by the Ballet Society with choreography by Jerome Robbins at the New York City Center on February 26, 1947.

title: Lamentable Figaro
summary: From "The Most Happy Fella", a musical composed by Leonard Bernstein, the song Lamentable Figaro is sung from the perspective of Tony's wife, Rosetta. The lyrics express her sadness and grief at having to leave him.

title: First Essay
summary: The First Essay is a piece for orchestra written by Samuel Barber in 1944, as the first of his three Essays for Orchestra. The work's premiere was given on April 7, 1944, at Carnegie Hall.

title: Second Essay
summary: The Second Piano Sonata by Samuel Barber, also known as the 'Piano Sonata' or 'Sonata for Piano', was written in 1935. It has four movements.

title: Third Essay
alternative_title: Third Essay for Orchestra: Op. 6 No. 3
summary: The Third Essay is a work by American composer Samuel Barber, written in 1944 and dedicated to his mother, Lucy Mae Barber. The piece features the use of a solo clarinet in the second movement, adding an emotive element to the overall sound.

title: Cello Concerto
summary: The Cello Concerto is a concerto for solo cello and orchestra composed by Samuel Barber. The work was written in the summer of 1945, during World War II. It is considered one of Barber's most famous works and has been widely performed around the world.

title: Medea's Dance of Vengeance
summary: Medea's Dance of Vengeance is a choral symphony by American composer Samuel Barber. Commissioned for the opening of the Academy of Music in Philadelphia, it premiered on December 18, 1955. The work is based on Euripides' play Medea, and its libretto was written by Dido Wilson.

title: A Setting of Heine's "Reiterstürz", Op. 41
summary: This work is a setting of a poem by Heinrich Heine, and it features a chorus accompanied by piano. The text describes the image of two horsemen crashing to the ground.

title: El Salon Mexico
summary: A three-movement orchestral suite that depicts Mexican folk life, El Salon Mexico was a major work for Copland in the late 1940s. The piece is based on themes and rhythms he heard during his own travels to Mexico in the early 1930s. It is considered one of his most popular works and is often performed at orchestral concerts.

title: Lincoln Portrait
summary: A portrait of President Abraham Lincoln, in the form of a symphony orchestra piece. The work is based on a poem by Carl Sandburg and features a speech by Lincoln from his second inaugural address.

title: Danse Russe (from Piano Variations)
summary: The Danse Russe is a movement from Aaron Copland's Piano Variations, composed in 1930-31. It is a highly rhythmic and energetic piece, evoking the sounds of Russian folk music. The work was commissioned by Harold Spivacke, head of the Music Division of the Library of Congress.

title: Vitebsk
summary: A slow and contemplative piece that evokes a sense of nostalgia and longing, inspired by the city of Vitebsk in Belarus. The melody is hauntingly beautiful, with a simple but effective harmony.

title: Redline Tango
summary: Redline Tango is a piece for piano and orchestra by American composer Aaron Copland, written in 1940. It was originally titled 'The Redline Rag' and was later renamed to avoid confusion with the well-known 'Tango in D Minor' by Rachmaninoff.

title: Hoedowns from Rodeo
summary: From the ballet score 'Rodeo', 'Hoedowns' is a high-energy piece featuring an energetic dance-like quality, showcasing Copland's unique blend of classical and American folk music elements. This piece showcases the rustic and lively spirit of America's Wild West.

title: Scherzo for Chamber Orchestra
summary: The Scherzo for Chamber Orchestra is a composition by Aaron Copland, written in 1952. It's part of his 'Dance Suite', but this particular piece is an orchestral work that features a scherzo (a lively and humorous section) with a strong rhythmic pulse. The music is playful, energetic and technically challenging for the performers.

title: Façade
summary: Façade, also known as Façade: Six Pieces for Orchestra, is a set of six orchestral movements composed by William Walton in 1922-23. The work was originally written to accompany seven poems by Edith Sitwell, which were first published in the collection 'Façade' in 1922.

title: A Mask of Time
summary: A Mask of Time is a work for solo violin and string orchestra written by William Walton in 1984. The piece was premiered on November 12, 1985, at the Royal Festival Hall in London.

title: Viola Concerto
summary: The Viola Concerto in A minor by William Walton is a concerto for viola and orchestra, written in 1929. It is considered one of the most technically challenging works for the viola and is notable for its virtuosic writing and lyricism.

title: Spitfire Prelude and Fugue
summary: The Spitfire Prelude and Fugue is a work for orchestra by William Walton, written in 1940 to commemorate the Hawker Hurricane and Supermarine Spitfire fighters. The piece is meant to evoke the spirit of the British people during World War II.

title: Orb and Sceptre
summary: Commissioned for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II, 'Coronation March' is a majestic work that combines grandeur with subtlety. The 'Orb and Sceptre' movement is a stately processional, while the 'Te Deum' is a rousing celebration of praise to God.

title: First Essay for Orchestra
summary: The First Essay in D major was composed in the spring of 1933 by William Walton. It is a short and energetic work, often described as a showcase for the orchestra's virtuosity.

title: A Ceremony of Carols
summary: A Ceremony of Carols is a choral work for boys' voices, written by Benjamin Britten in 1942. It was commissioned by the London Boys' Choir and was first performed at Cambridge University on Christmas Eve 1943. The work is based on medieval carols and folk songs from various parts of England, arranged in a loose narrative framework to evoke the atmosphere of an old-fashioned Christmas celebration.

title: The Rape of Lucretia
summary: Britten's opera 'The Rape of Lucretia' is a poignant retelling of the ancient Roman legend. The music is characterized by its intense emotional depth and complexity, evoking feelings of sadness and despair.

title: Albert Herring
summary: A comic opera in three acts, based on the 1919 novel of the same name by Guy Bolton and P.G. Wodehouse. The story revolves around Albert Herring, a young man from a respectable family who is forced to marry a woman he doesn't love. Albert's rebellion against societal expectations is the central theme of the opera.

title: Les Illuminations
summary: Setting of Arthur Rimbaud's poetry, Les Illuminations is a song cycle for soprano and piano. The piece is a poignant exploration of love, loss, and the fleeting nature of human experience. Britten's music is characterized by its lyricism, expressiveness, and emotional depth.

title: Nocturne Op. 60
summary: Nocturne for Piano in E-flat major, Op. 55, No. 4, and Nocturne for Piano in F-sharp minor, Op. 48, No. 2 are pieces that Britten wrote early in his career.

title: Phantasy Quartet
summary: The Phantasy Quartets, Op. 25, are two works for string quartet by Benjamin Britten, composed in 1932. They are a key work of the English musical renaissance and demonstrate Britten's mastery of traditional forms.

title: Serenade for Tenor, Horn and Strings
summary: This serenade was written by Benjamin Britten in 1943. It is a piece of classical music for tenor voice, horn, and strings. The work is based on nine poems from Michelangelo's sonnets. The serenade is known for its lyricism, expressiveness, and technical demands.

title: The Dream of Gerontius
summary: A setting of John Henry Newman's poem, the oratorio describes a person's journey through life and death. The dreamer is confronted with his own mortality and ultimately finds peace.

title: Enigma Variations
summary: The Enigma Variations, Op. 36, is a set of musical variations for orchestra by Edward Elgar. It was written in the summer of 1898 and dedicated to A.J. Jaeger, who had been the inspiration behind it. The work is dedicated 'To my friends represented here', with each variation being a portrait of someone close to Elgar.

title: Sospiri (Elegy for Strings)
summary: Sospiri, also known as the Elegy for Strings, is a composition by Edward Elgar. It was written in 1903 and first performed at the Three Choirs Festival held in Gloucester Cathedral on September 23, 1904. The piece is a slow and contemplative lament for strings, evoking feelings of sadness and introspection.

title: Pomp and Circumstance March No. 2
summary: The Pomp and Circumstance Marches are a series of marches written by Sir Edward Elgar between 1901 and 1930. The first march, in D major, was commissioned for the coronation of King Edward VII. Elgar continued to write marches on various occasions, including the coronation of George V, and these were published together as "The Crown Imperial". The March No. 2 is one of the most popular and well-known pieces from this series.

title: Violin Concerto in B minor, Op. 61
summary: The Violin Concerto in B minor, Op. 61 is a concertante work for violin and orchestra written by Edward Elgar between 1909 and 1910. The concerto was revised several times before its first performance in New York City in 1918.

title: Imperial March
summary: The Pomp and Circumstance Marches are a series of five marches composed by Edward Elgar, each associated with a particular circumstance or occasion. The first march was written in 1901 for the coronation of King Edward VII of the United Kingdom.

title: Fantasia on a Theme by Thomas Tallis
summary: A choral work based on the theme of Thomas Tallis's 'Spem in Alium', written for the bicentenary of the composer's death. It is a celebration of the beauty and harmony of nature, with lyrics by Ursula Knight.

title: Dona Nobis Pacem
summary: A setting of a psalm by Vaughan Williams, featuring the chorus and soloists. The work is an expression of hope for peace in troubled times.

title: Symphony No. 8
summary: The Symphony No. 8 in D minor by Ralph Vaughan Williams is a large-scale symphonic work composed between 1949 and 1955. It was his first major composition since World War II and represents his return to form after the trauma of the war.

title: A Sea Symphony (Sailing)
summary: A Sea Symphony, also known as A Song of the Sea, is a choral symphony by Ralph Vaughan Williams. It was commissioned for the centenary of the National Maritime Museum in Greenwich, London and premiered on June 7, 1909, at the Queen's Hall, London. The work sets Walt Whitman's poem 'A Noiseless Patient Spider' and uses words from old sea shanties to evoke the spirit of the sea.

title: Toward the Unknown Region
summary: Toward the Unknown Region, Op. 132, is a symphonic poem composed by Ralph Vaughan Williams in 1958. The work was written for the centenary of the Royal Philharmonic Society and its premiere took place on March 25, 1958, at the Queen's Hall in London, with the composer conducting the London Symphony Orchestra.

title: Norfolk Rhapsody No. 1
summary: The Norfolk Rhapsodies are two large-scale orchestral works composed by Ralph Vaughan Williams between 1906 and 1918, with the first movement of the First Rhapsody completed in 1906. The work is a setting of traditional folk songs from Norfolk, with complex harmonies and rhythms reflecting the composer's interest in folk music.

title: The Birds
summary: The Birds is a tone poem by Ottorino Respighi, composed in 1928. It is part of his collection of Italian landscapes, together with The Pines of Rome and Fountains of Rome. The piece is written for large orchestra without solo instruments and depicts the sounds that might be heard in the countryside, such as birdsong.

title: Belkis, Queen of Sheba
summary: The suite 'Belkis, Queen of Sheba' is a musical composition by Italian composer Ottorino Respighi. The work is inspired by the ancient legend of the Queen of Sheba and her encounter with King Solomon. The suite is structured in five movements: I. Introitus (Introduction), II. Ballo (Ball), III. Coro e scherzo, IV. Aria del Re (King's Aria) and V. Adagio.

title: Adagio for Strings (arrangement of a portion of his arrangement of the music from 'Messa da Requiem' by Luigi Cherubini)
summary: Respighi's Adagio for Strings is a piece of orchestral music arranged from his own setting of the Requiem Mass by Luigi Cherubini. The work was composed in 1914 and was first performed in that year by the Bologna Opera Orchestra, conducted by Respighi himself.

title: Ancient Airs and Dances Suite No. 1
summary: The Ancient Airs and Dances Suite No. 1 is a suite for orchestra by Ottorino Respighi, composed in 1916. It is the first of three suites that Respighi wrote based on 16th-century Italian lute music.

title: Ancient Airs and Dances Suite No. 3
summary: The Ancient Airs and Dances Suite No. 3 is a suite for orchestra composed by Ottorino Respighi, based on Renaissance melodies from the Italian and French courts of the 16th century. The work was written in 1922-23, but published posthumously in 1930.

title: The Three Botticelli Pictures
summary: The Three Botticellis is a suite for orchestra, Ottorino Respighi's final large-scale work. It is inspired by Sandro Botticelli's paintings Primavera and The Birth of Venus. The work consists of three movements, each representing one of the paintings.

title: Danze Sinfoniche
summary: The Danze Sinfoniche (Symphonic Dances) are three orchestral suites by Ottorino Respighi, composed between 1917 and 1935. The work is considered one of Respighi's most important compositions, showcasing his mastery of orchestration and musical structure.

title: Metamorfosi d'Oreste
summary: The Metamorphosis of Orestes (Italian: Metamorfosi d'Oreste) is a symphonic poem by Ottorino Respighi, composed in 1916. The work is based on the ancient Greek legend of Orestes and Electra. The piece is divided into four sections, each depicting a different aspect of the mythological story. The music is characterized by its intense drama and emotional depth, showcasing Respighi's mastery of orchestration.

title: Dance of the Knights
summary: The 'Dance of the Knights' is a famous piece from Prokofiev's ballet 'Romeo and Juliet'. It is an energetic and dramatic representation of the duel between Tybalt and Romeo. The music features a series of complex rhythms and melodies that create a sense of tension and conflict.

title: Romeo and Juliet: Montagues and Capulets
summary: This piece is the overture to Prokofiev's famous ballet 'Romeo and Juliet', based on Shakespeare's play. It sets the tone for the tragic love story, combining elements of classical music with a touch of modernity.

title: Alexander Nevsky: Korteke Laulu
summary: Korteke Laulu (Short Hymn) is a movement from Sergei Prokofiev's cantata 'Alexander Nevsky'. The cantata was written in 1939 to commemorate the heroism of Alexander Nevsky, a medieval prince who defended Russia against Teutonic invasions. This specific track features a choral piece set to the lyrics of the hymn 'Molitva o Spasiteli' (Prayer to the Savior). The music is characterized by Prokofiev's signature blend of Soviet patriotism and classical influences, resulting in a grandiose and atmospheric sound.

title: Lieutenant Kije: The Burial of Kije
summary: The Lieutenant Kije suite is a set of five orchestral pieces that tell the story of an imaginary officer, Lieutenant Kije. The Burial of Kije is the fourth movement in the suite and features a mournful and elegiac melody.

title: Symphony No. 7, IV Allegro giocoso
alternative_title: Symphony No. 7 in C-sharp minor, IV Allegro giocoso
summary: The fourth movement of the symphony is an allegro giocoso, a lively and playful finale. The theme is introduced by the piccolo in a rhythmic pattern that is repeated and varied throughout the movement.

title: Violin Concerto No. 2: Andantino
summary: The Second Violin Concerto, Op. 64, is a concerto for solo violin and orchestra by Sergei Prokofiev. Composed in 1935, it is considered one of the most technically demanding concertos written for the instrument. The work consists of three movements: Allegro moderato, Adagio, and Andantino.

title: Cinderella: Waltz
summary: The Cinderella Suite, Op. 87, is a ballet score composed by Sergei Prokofiev in 1944. The suite is based on the fairy tale 'Cinderella' and features six movements, including the Waltz.

title: Romeo and Juliet: Love Duet
alternative_title: Romeo and Juliet: Love Duet (The Balcony Scene)
summary: From the ballet 'Romeo and Juliet', Op. 75, this love duet is one of the most famous scenes in classical music.

title: Five Melodies for Piano
summary: The Five Melodies, Op. 35, are a set of five piano pieces written by Sergei Prokofiev in 1930-1931. They are known for their simplicity and innocence.

title: Boléro
summary: Bolero is a famous orchestral work by French composer Maurice Ravel, written in 1928. The piece begins with a simple melody and gradually builds up to a dramatic climax. Bolero is known for its hypnotic rhythm and repetitive theme, creating a sense of tension and anticipation.

title: Daphnis et Chloé: Suite No. 2, M. 90 - II. Danse générale
summary: The second suite from Maurice Ravel's ballet score Daphnis et Chloé is a symphonic work that showcases the composer's mastery of orchestration and his ability to evoke the beauty and drama of ancient Greece. The second movement, Danse générale, is a lively and energetic piece that features a large orchestra and a range of percussion instruments.

title: La Valse
summary: La Valse is a piano piece by Maurice Ravel, composed in 1906. It is based on the traditional Viennese waltz and features complex harmonies and rhythms. The music depicts the decay of the aristocracy in Austria during World War I.

title: Mother Goose Suite: III. Petit Poucet
summary: The 'Mother Goose' suite by Maurice Ravel is a musical interpretation of six nursery rhymes by Charles Perrault and the Brothers Grimm. The third movement, 'Petit Poucet', is based on a story about a young boy who saves his family from poverty with his wit and cunning. This movement features a lively and energetic theme, evoking the sense of adventure and triumph.

title: Don Quichotte à Dulcinée
summary: Prelude to Don Quixote, a musical composition by Maurice Ravel, is based on the novel of the same name by Miguel de Cervantes. The piece is scored for solo cello and features the famous opening phrase, known as 'Don Quichotte à Dulcinée'. This lyrical melody is meant to evoke the sadness and longing that Don Quixote feels towards his lady love Dulcinea.

title: Rapsodie espagnole - I. Praludium
summary: The Rapsodie Espagnole is a suite of orchestral pieces by French composer Maurice Ravel, based on folk melodies from various parts of Spain. The first movement, Praludium, is an energetic and lively piece that captures the spirit of Spanish music.

title: Miroirs: II. Oiseaux tristes
summary: Oiseaux Tristes (Unhappy Birds) is a movement from Maurice Ravel's piano suite Miroirs. It evokes the sorrow of birds who have lost their homes, reflecting Ravel's own melancholic feelings during World War I.

title: String Quartet in F major, M. 35 - IV. Allegretto scherzando
summary: The String Quartet in F major is a work for string quartet by Maurice Ravel. It was composed in 1902-1903 and premiered in 1904. The fourth movement, Allegretto scherzando, is characterized by its lively and playful rhythm.

title: Carnival of the Animals
summary: The Carnival of the Animals is a humorous suite composed by Camille Saint-Saëns, written for two pianos and an orchestra. The work was intended as a joke, but it has become one of the most popular orchestral works in the classical music repertoire. It consists of 14 movements, each representing different animals, such as birds, reptiles, mammals, and fish.

title: The Swan
summary: The Swan is a famous cello piece from the Carnival of the Animals suite. It features a beautiful and lyrical melody that evokes the image of a swan gliding effortlessly across a lake.

title: Spring Song
summary: The Spring Song, also known as Printemps for orchestra, is a symphonic poem composed by Camille Saint-Saëns in 1871. The piece is characterized by its lighthearted and lively melody, evoking the feeling of spring.

title: The Entombment
summary: The Entombment, Op. 4, is a choral symphony by Camille Saint-Saëns. It was composed in 1859 and revised several times before its publication in 1875. The work is a setting of the burial of Christ from the Gospel according to John.

title: Marche Militaire Française
summary: The Marche Militaire Française is a military march for band written by Camille Saint-Saëns. The piece was composed in 1878 and is known for its lively and energetic rhythm, making it perfect for military parades and other patriotic events.

title: Le Rêve
summary: One of the most famous pieces for solo piano, Le Rêve is a beautiful and dreamy nocturne that evokes the feeling of being lost in a peaceful and serene world. The piece features a lilting melody that seems to dance across the keys, accompanied by delicate arpeggios and subtle dynamic contrasts.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2
summary: The Piano Concerto No. 2 in G minor, Op. 22 is a concerto for piano and orchestra composed by Camille Saint-Saëns. The work was dedicated to the pianist Alphonse Hartmann and premiered on March 5, 1869, with the composer at the piano.

title: Carnaval des Animaux: Hymne à Nimue
summary: Hymne à Nimue is the final piece from Satie's 'Carnaval des Animaux', a set of pieces for solo piano. It is characterized by its lighthearted and playful nature, evoking a sense of whimsy and fantasy.

title: Gymnopédie No. 2
summary: The Gymnopédie No. 2 is a piece for solo piano, the second of three compositions by Erik Satie, published in 1888. The composition is characterized by a slow and peaceful melody, with a minimalist structure and repetition.

title: Gnossienne No. 3
summary: The Gnossiennes are a set of six short pieces for solo piano composed by Erik Satie between 1890 and 1903. The Gnossienne No. 3 is the third piece in this set and is known for its dreamy, languid quality. It features a simple, repetitive melody that evokes a sense of longing or nostalgia.

title: Cinq Grimaces pour "Le Fantôme du Parc"
alternative_title: Cinq Grimaces pour 'Le Fantôme du Parc'
summary: Cinq grimaces pour 'Le fantôme du parc' is a short piece for piano by French composer Erik Satie. The work, which consists of five short sections, was written in 1917 and is part of Satie's oeuvre known as Musique d'ameublement (furniture music). The composition is intended to be played softly, without great musical skill, and to create a soothing atmosphere.

title: Trois Morceaux en forme de Poèmes: Danse Useless
summary: Trois Morceaux en forme de Poèmes is a set of three piano pieces composed by Erik Satie in 1913. The title Danse Useless is one of the three movements, which are meant to be performed in any order or simultaneously. The music is characterized by a minimalist and repetitive style, with a focus on musical simplicity and a rejection of traditional classical forms.

title: Vexations
summary: Vexations is a piano piece written by Erik Satie in 1893, consisting of only 12 repetitive chords. The piece was originally intended as an exercise in monotony and simplicity, with the composer suggesting that it be repeated 840 times.

title: Sinfonie in G minor
summary: The Symphony in G minor, Sinfonie in G minor, is a symphony by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It was composed between 1845 and 1852 and dedicated to the King of Sweden. The work is notable for its innovative use of harmony and its exploration of complex themes and structures.

title: Sinfonie in C major
summary: The Sinfonie in C major, Op. 10 is a symphony written by Franz Berwald, composed between 1848 and 1850, but not published until 1865.

title: Sinfonie in B flat major
summary: The Sinfonie in B-flat major, Op. 11 is a symphony by Swedish composer Franz Berwald, written between 1846 and 1855. It is considered one of the most important works of the Swedish Romantic period. The symphony has four movements: Allegro con fuoco, Adagio sostenuto, Scherzo - Allegro molto, and Finale: Allegro risoluto.

title: Romances for Violin and Orchestra
summary: The Romances for Violin and Orchestra, Op. 23, are a set of four movements composed by Swedish composer Franz Berwald in 1847. The work is considered one of the most important contributions to the violin repertoire during the Romantic era.

title: Overture to "Estelle"
summary: The Overture to Estelle was written by Franz Berwald in 1849. It is a classical symphonic piece, part of his larger work 'Estelle' (Sinfonie Es-dur, op. 28). The overture is a typical example of the late Romantic period's influence on classical music.

title: Overture to "Eurante"
summary: The Overture to Eurante is a classical music composition by Franz Berwald. It's the opening movement of his opera Eurante, written in 1852-53. This piece features the dramatic and expressive qualities typical of Berwald's works.

title: Suite in D minor
alternative_title: Sinfonia Grossa: Suite in D minor
summary: The Sinfonia Grossa, also known as the Grande Symphonie Militaire, is a symphony by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It was composed in 1845 and is considered one of his most popular works.

title: Caprice for Solo Piano
summary: The Caprice in D-flat major, Op. 4, No. 2 is a capriccio for solo piano by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It was composed around 1829-1830 and published posthumously in 1863.

title: Serenade for Strings
summary: The Serenade for Strings in A major, Op. 3, is a work by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It was written in 1848 and is considered one of his most popular works.

title: Sinfonietta in G minor
summary: The Sinfonietta in G minor is a symphonic work by Swedish composer Franz Berwald. It was composed in 1845 and premiered the same year in Stockholm. The piece is characterized by its lyrical and expressive melodies, as well as its innovative use of harmony and structure.

title: Impromptu in A-flat major
summary: The Impromptus (German: Impromptus) Op. posth. 142, D. 899 are a set of four piano pieces written by Franz Schubert in 1827. The set includes two impromptus and two other movements. The piece marked 'Andante' is the most well known among them.

title: Gretchen am Spinnrade
summary: Gretchen am Spinnrade is a song written by Franz Schubert in 1814, based on the poem of the same name by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe. The song tells the story of Gretchen, who is sitting at her spinning wheel and thinking about her lover. She is caught between her love for him and her sense of duty to her family. The song is a beautiful example of Schubert's ability to set poetry to music and bring out the emotional depth of the words.

title: Wanderer Fantasy
summary: The Wanderer Fantasy is a piano piece composed by Franz Schubert in 1822, during his final illness. It is one of the last works he composed and was first published posthumously. The fantasy consists of five movements and features a range of moods and emotions, from introspective to dramatic.

title: Impromptu in E-flat major
summary: Impromptu in E-flat major, Op. 142, No. 2 is a piano piece written by Franz Schubert in 1827. It is the second of four impromptus for solo piano composed during his final year of life. The music is characterized by its serene and contemplative mood, with a gentle lyricism that sets it apart from other works of the Classical period.

title: Moment Musical in F minor
summary: The 'Moments Musicaux' are six short piano pieces written by Franz Schubert. They were composed in 1823 and first published posthumously. The piece in F minor is the third of the set, marked 'Allegro moderato'. It has a lively but melancholic character, with arpeggios and broken chord patterns giving it a sense of forward momentum.

title: Piano Quintet in A major
summary: The Piano Quintet in A major, D.667 (also known as Trout Quintet), is a work for piano and string quartet by Franz Schubert. It was composed in August 1819 during the composer's summer stay in Steyrling. The quintet consists of four movements: Allegro, Andante, Scherzo: Presto, and Allegretto. It is considered one of Schubert's most popular and technically challenging chamber music works.

title: Die Winterreise
summary: Die Winterreise is a song cycle for solo voice and piano composed by Franz Schubert in 1827. The cycle consists of 24 songs, each with its own unique poem. The lyrics are taken from the poems of Wilhelm Müller's collection "Winterreise" which describe a journey through the harsh winter landscape.

title: Erlkönig
summary: A musical setting of Goethe's poem, the song tells the story of a father who is trying to comfort his dying son. The poem describes the child as being cold and pale, while his father tries to reassure him that he will soon be warm again.

title: Sunrise
summary: Sunrise is an oratorio composed by Franz Joseph Haydn in 1791. The work is a musical setting of the biblical account of creation, with text from the Book of Genesis.

title: Symphony No. 94, "Surprise"
summary: The Symphony No. 94 in G major is a symphony by Franz Joseph Haydn, composed in 1791. It is part of his famous "London" series and known for its surprise finale, which abruptly shifts from a calm, serene theme to an energetic, lively one.

title: String Quartet Op. 76, No. 3
summary: The String Quartets Op. 76 are a set of six string quartets by Joseph Haydn, composed in 1796-1797. They were dedicated to King George III. The third quartet is one of the most popular and well-known among them.

title: London Symphony No. 104
summary: The 'London Symphonies' are a series of nine symphonies by Haydn, composed in 1791-1792 and published in London. They were written for performance at the salons of the aristocracy in England. No. 104 is one of the most popular works from this collection.

title: The Creation
summary: Oratorio in three parts, written for the Eszterházy family and first performed at their castle in 1799. The work is a setting of Paradise Lost by John Milton and tells the story of creation from the Book of Genesis.

title: Piano Sonata in C major (Hob. XVI:50)
summary: The Piano Sonata in C major, Hob. XVI:50 is a sonata for solo piano composed by Joseph Haydn. It was published in 1787 and consists of three movements: Allegro con spirito, Adagio cantabile, and Allegro assai.

title: Harp Concerto in E flat major
summary: The Harp Concerto in E-flat major, Hob. XVII:4 is a concertino for harp and orchestra by Austrian composer Franz Joseph Haydn. It was composed around 1784-1785, during the Classical period. The concerto is considered one of Haydn's most notable works for solo harp.

title: Trumpet Concerto in E flat major
summary: The Trumpet Concerto in E-flat major, Hob. VIIe:1, is a concerto for trumpet and orchestra by Franz Joseph Haydn. The work is considered one of the most important pieces in the classical trumpet repertoire. It is scored for solo trumpet, strings, and continuo.

title: Pianoforte Concerto in D major
summary: The Pianoforte Concerto in D major is a concerto for piano and orchestra written by Franz Joseph Haydn. It is considered one of the earliest concertos to be written for this combination of instruments. The concerto consists of three movements, each with its own unique character and mood. The first movement is allegro, featuring a lively and energetic melody, while the second movement is adagio, showcasing a more romantic and contemplative tone. The final movement is allegretto, characterized by a playful and carefree atmosphere.

title: "The Seasons"
summary: The Seasons is a set of piano pieces composed by Ludwig van Beethoven, but it was actually arranged by Franz Liszt from the poem cycle by Alexander Pushkin with music originally created for piano by Joseph Haydn. The work is known as one of the most original and creative compositions in classical music.

title: The Barber of Seville - Overture
summary: The Barber of Seville is an opera buffa in two acts by Gioachino Rossini, with an Italian libretto by Cesare Sterbini. The opera is based on Pierre Beaumarchais's French play Le Barbier de Séville, which is set in the 18th century and tells the story of a young nobleman named Almaviva who falls in love with a beautiful young woman named Rosina.

title: La Cenerentola - Polacca dei ballerini
summary: The Polacca dei Ballerini is a famous polka-like dance from the opera 'La Cenerentola' by Gioachino Rossini. The music is lively and energetic, with a catchy melody that showcases the virtuosity of the dancers.

title: Il Barbiere di Siviglia - Largo al factotum
summary: The 'Largo al Factotum' is a famous aria from the opera Il Barbiere di Siviglia, composed by Gioachino Rossini. The aria is sung by the character Figaro, who is describing his various tasks and responsibilities as a barber and factotum (a person who does everything). The music is known for its complex rhythm and melodic passages, making it a showcase for the singer's vocal skills.

title: Tancredi - Di tanti palpiti
summary: Tancredi is an opera in two acts by Gioachino Rossini, based on the play Tancred by Augustin-Joseph Carrel. The libretto was written by Gaetano Rossi, and the music was composed between March 1819 and January 1820. Di tanti palpiti is one of the most famous arias from the opera, sung by the character Amenaide in Act I.

title: Semiramide - Bel raggio lusinghieri
summary: Bel raggio lusinghieri is a famous aria from the opera Semiramide by Gioachino Rossini. The aria is sung by the character Arsace and is known for its virtuosic vocal demands and beautiful melodies. The lyrics describe the beauty of the moon and the singer's longing to be reunited with his beloved.

title: Armida - Qual cor trionfai
summary: Armida - Qual cor trionfai is an aria from the opera Armida by Gioachino Rossini. It is a famous and iconic piece of music that showcases Rossini's mastery of vocal writing. The aria features a beautiful and complex melody, with intricate ornamentation and dramatic flair. The lyrics are taken from Torquato Tasso's epic poem Gerusalemme Liberata and describe Armida's lament for her lost love.

title: La Donna del Lago - Ah! non son ingannato
summary: La Donna del Lago (The Lady of the Lake) is an opera in three acts by Gioachino Rossini. The music is considered to be one of Rossini's most expressive and romantic works. Ah! non son ingannato is a duet sung by Selica and Malcom, where they express their love for each other.

title: Le siège de Corinthe - Scena d'amore
summary: The Siege of Corinth is an opera in four acts by Gioachino Rossini. The libretto was written by Alexandre Soumet, based on a scenario by Prosper-Philippe Couvé and Henri Grétry. This piece is considered one of Rossini's last operas to be performed during his lifetime.

title: Stabat Mater - O quam tranquilla
summary: The 'Stabat Mater' is a work by Gioachino Rossini, composed in 1831. The piece was written for four soloists and chorus and is set to the poetry of Giovanni Battista Perbellini's text. It is scored for two violins, viola, cello, double basses, oboe, clarinet, horn and harp.

title: Symphonie Fantastique: I. Reveries - Passions
summary: The work is a musical representation of the composer's own dreams and emotions, structured into five distinct movements.

title: Symphonie Fantastique: II. A Ball
summary: The second movement of Berlioz's 'Symphonie Fantastique' is a depiction of a ball, with the orchestra representing the music and laughter of the partygoers. The movement is characterized by its lighthearted and playful nature, with a sense of carefree joy.

title: Symphonie Fantastique: III. Scene in the Marketplace
summary: The third movement of the 'Symphonie Fantastique' is a depiction of a crowded marketplace on market day, with the sounds of vendors calling out their wares. The music features a lively melody with a sense of nervous energy, as if the listener is being swept up in the excitement of the scene.

title: Symphonie Fantastique: IV. March to the Scaffold
summary: The fourth movement of Berlioz's Symphonie Fantastique is a dramatic and ominous representation of a public execution, complete with a funeral march and a sudden, violent outburst. The movement is often referred to as the 'Scene de la guillotine' or the 'Marche au supplice'. It is based on the real-life execution of Robert Ferdinand Dussaut, who was guillotined in Paris in 1825.

title: Symphonie Fantastique: V. Dream of a Witches' Sabbath
summary: The final movement is an epic depiction of a witches' sabbath, with a haunting melody played on the solo violin and accompanied by the full orchestra. The music is characterized by dark, ominous timbres and complex rhythms.

title: Romeo and Juliet Overture
summary: The Romeo and Juliet Overture is a symphonic poem composed by Hector Berlioz in 1839. The work is based on William Shakespeare's play Romeo and Juliet and depicts the tragic love story of the two young lovers. The overture is a grand and dramatic score that captures the passion, romance, and ultimately, the sorrow of the couple's doomed relationship.

title: Harold en Italie - II. Scherzo
summary: Harold en Italie is a symphonic poem, composed by Hector Berlioz in 1834. The work was written for viola and orchestra. It is in four movements: Largo (Allegro), Allegretto, Scherzo, and Finale.

title: Te Deum: III. Et in unum Dominum
summary: The Te Deum is a sacred choral work by French composer Hector Berlioz, written to commemorate Napoleon's victory at the Battle of Wagram in 1809. The piece consists of seven movements and features a chorus and orchestra.

title: Lelio, or The Return to Life
summary: L'elu du royaume des cieux (The Eleventh of September) is a dramatic oratorio composed by Hector Berlioz. It was composed in 1830 and revised in 1856, after which it became more well-known. The oratorio was dedicated to the memory of Berlioz's beloved friend, the poet Jacques Delille.

title: Aragonesa
summary: The Aragonesa (or Spanish Suite) is a piano suite by Isaac Albéniz, composed in 1887-88. It consists of six movements: Preludio, Romance, Mazurka, Espana, Zapateado and Andaluza. The piece showcases Albéniz's unique style of blending Spanish folk elements with classical music.

title: Cordobesca
summary: The piece evokes the charm and beauty of Andalusian culture, with a lively rhythm and melodic motifs reminiscent of Spanish folk music. It is part of Albéniz's "Suite Española".

title: Albeniz: Asturias (Bachianas)
summary: Asturias is a piece of music by Spanish composer Isaac Albéniz, part of the suite 'España' (also known as 'Suite Española'). It's inspired by the folk melodies from Asturias in northern Spain. The piece features intricate piano arpeggios and a lilting rhythm that evokes the feeling of traditional Spanish dance.

title: Valencia
summary: The work is a piano piece in six sections, depicting scenes and moods associated with the city of Valencia. The sections are: Prelude (Albaicin), Solea, Villancico, Polo, Fiesta, and Adagio.

title: Espana
summary: Asturias (Leyenda) by Isaac Albéniz, composed in 1884-86, is a famous piece from the suite 'España'. The music evokes images of Spanish folklore and is characterized by a dreamy and melancholic mood. It's considered one of Albéniz's most popular works.

title: Puerta de Tierra
summary: From the suite 'España', this piece is a beautiful and evocative portrayal of the Puerta de Tierra in Madrid, Spain. The music conjures up images of a warm summer evening, with the sound of gentle waves lapping against the shore.

title: Cadenza
summary: Asturias (Leyenda) is a piece for piano by Isaac Albéniz, composed in 1890-1892. It is part of the suite "Suite Española". The title 'Asturias' refers to the region of Asturias in northern Spain.

title: Concierto de Aranjuez: Adagio
summary: The Concierto de Aranjuez is a guitar concerto written by Joaquín Rodrigo in 1939. The Adagio movement, also known as the 'Adagio for Guitar and Orchestra', is one of the most famous pieces from this work. It is characterized by its serene and peaceful atmosphere, evoking the beauty of the garden of the Duke of Villamanrique's palace in Aranjuez.

title: Concierto de Aranjuez: Allegro
summary: The Concierto de Aranjuez is a concerto for classical guitar and orchestra, composed by Joaquín Rodrigo. The work was commissioned by the Spanish guitarist Regino Sainz de la Maza and dedicated to him. The concerto is in three movements: Allegro, Adagio, and Allegrissimo.

title: Concierto de Aranjuez: Adagio (Sarabanda)
summary: The Concierto de Aranjuez is a concerto for classical guitar and orchestra by Joaquín Rodrigo. The Adagio, also known as the Sarabanda, is the second movement of this concerto. It is considered one of the most technically challenging pieces for classical guitar.

title: Invocation to the Muses
summary: A piece for solo guitar, written in 1939 and premiered in 1941. It is considered one of the most technically challenging and beautiful pieces for classical guitar.

title: Tonadilla Estupenda
summary: The Tonadilla Estupenda, also known as the "Wonderful Folksong", is a composition for solo piano by Spanish composer Joaquín Rodrigo. It was written in 1964 and is part of his suite Tonadillas.

title: A los árboles
summary: A los árboles (To the Trees) is a piece for guitar and orchestra written by Joaquín Rodrigo. The work, dedicated to Andrés Segovia, is characterized by its melancholic and introspective mood. It consists of three movements: Allegro, Interludio y final. A los árboles premiered in 1949 at the Palacio de la Música Catalana in Barcelona.

title: Tres piezas para orquesta: Elegía

title: Suite española No. 1: Los tarantos
